articles.title: La WNBA sigue pisando charcos con la polémica trans: "Tapa esa camiseta o te vas"
articles.standfirst: Obliga a varios aficionados a tapar sus camisetas con menciones a la controversia cultural trans durante un partido y luego pide perdón
articles.summary: Obliga a varios aficionados a tapar sus camisetas con menciones a la controversia cultural trans durante un partido y luego pide perdón
articles.body: La WNBA vuelve a estar en el centro de la batalla cultural en Estados Unidos. Al menos tres aficionados fueron requeridos por personal de seguridad para cubrir camisetas con mensajes relacionados con la participación de mujeres trans en el deporte femenino durante el partido entre Atlanta Dream e Indiana Fever, según informó Fox News. La propia liga reconoció posteriormente que la actuación fue un error y dejó claro que los espectadores deberían haber podido mostrar sus prendas. Entre los afectados se encontraban Kasey Thomason y su hija Annie, que acudieron al State Farm Arena con camisetas de XX-XY Athletics, organización que defiende que las categorías deportivas femeninas estén reservadas a personas asignadas como mujeres al nacer. Ambas habían comprado entradas a apenas dos filas de la pista y permanecieron en sus localidades durante prácticamente todo el encuentro sin incidentes. La situación cambió durante la prórroga. Según su relato, un miembro de seguridad les pidió que abandonaran sus asientos y les comunicó que algunos aficionados se habían sentido ofendidos por sus camisetas. Las opciones que recibieron fueron ponerse una camiseta del Atlanta Dream o abandonar el pabellón. "¿La biología y la ciencia son ofensivas?", respondió Kasey antes de aceptar, a regañadientes, la camiseta del equipo local para poder presenciar los últimos minutos. Las imágenes de ESPN mostraron a madre e hija con las nuevas prendas durante la recta final de un partido que terminó con victoria de Indiana por 95-91. Las Thomason aseguran que otros espectadores les mostraron su apoyo y sospechan que una aficionada que lucía un mensaje favorable a los derechos de las personas trans pudo alertar a la seguridad, aunque no pudieron confirmar que esa fuera la causa de la intervención. El episodio ha abierto además un debate sobre los límites de la libertad de expresión en las gradas. El reglamento del State Farm Arena restringe prendas con lenguaje explícito, blasfemias o mensajes despectivos, mientras que las normas de conducta de la NBA contemplan también determinadas expresiones obscenas o indecentes. Sin embargo, las protagonistas sostienen que el argumento que recibieron de los responsables de seguridad fue que sus camisetas eran simplemente "ofensivas". La controversia se produce en un momento especialmente delicado para la WNBA, que debate sus criterios de elegibilidad para las mujeres transgénero. Nunca ha habido una jugadora trans en la competición y el convenio colectivo establece que la liga está reservada a mujeres, pero no especifica el sexo asignado al nacer ni establece una política concreta sobre identidad de género. Además, el incidente de Atlanta no es un caso aislado. Apenas unas semanas antes, dos adolescentes que vestían prendas de XX-XY protagonizaron otro enfrentamiento en un partido de la WNBA que acabó con la suspensión durante cinco encuentros y una sanción económica para Celeste Keaton, copropietaria de Seattle Storm. Las camisetas de esta organización se han convertido así en uno de los símbolos de una batalla cultural que trasciende cada vez más las propias canchas. La WNBA ha intentado cerrar la polémica admitiendo que sus responsables de seguridad se equivocaron y comunicando a los encargados del partido que los aficionados no deberían haber sido obligados a ocultar sus mensajes. El Atlanta Dream también se desmarcó de lo ocurrido y aseguró que no participó en la decisión. Pero el episodio vuelve a colocar a la liga en el epicentro de un debate que mezcla deporte, libertad de expresión, identidad de género y protección de las categorías femeninas, una tormenta que amenaza con seguir creciendo alrededor de la WNBA.

articles.title: Un Barça que ya no parece el Barça
articles.standfirst: Histórica catarsis azulgrana con 11 salidas, 9 fichajes y un nuevo entrenador para evitar el cuarto curso consecutivo en blanco
articles.summary: Histórica catarsis azulgrana con 11 salidas, 9 fichajes y un nuevo entrenador para evitar el cuarto curso consecutivo en blanco
articles.body: El Barça ha pulsado el botón de reseteo, tan socorrido en los aparatos electrónicos que dejan de funcionar para borrar su configuración y dejarlo en su estado original de fábrica, y el resultado ha sido la mayor catarsis en la historia reciente de la sección. Su nuevo director deportivo, Xevi Pujol, como si de un jefe de mantenimiento se tratase, ha sido el encargado de 'restaurar' el sistema que tan mal funcionaba, depurando la plantilla con once salidas, nueve fichajes y un nuevo entrenador. Una reconstrucción sin precedentes en un club obligado a romper con la etapa más frustrante de la última década. El objetivo es tan claro como urgente: evitar un cuarto año consecutivo sin títulos. El tercer curso seguido en blanco ha sido la gota que ha colmado el vaso. El balance desde la temporada 2013-14 retrata una caída difícil de imaginar en un gigante europeo del calibre del azulgrana: apenas dos Ligas Endesa y cuatro Copas del Rey en doce campañas. Un botín ínfimo para un escudo acostumbrado a pelear por todo. La inestabilidad tampoco ha dado tregua en los despachos ni en el banquillo. Ocho entrenadores y cuatro directores deportivos en doce años reflejan un proyecto que ha ido apagando fuegos sin encontrar una dirección definitiva. Ni Pesic, ni Jasikevicius, ni el regreso de Xavi Pascual lograron devolver al Barça a la cima de Europa. Ahora le toca el turno a Aleksandar Sekulic, llamado a liderar una revolución de enorme calado. La marcha de Xavi Pascual rumbo al Dubai Basketball simboliza el cierre definitivo de un ciclo que tampoco encontró el camino del éxito. El técnico esloveno hereda un vestuario prácticamente irreconocible. La lista de despedidas impresiona por cantidad y peso específico. Se han marchado Willy Hernangómez, Satoransky, Laprovittola, Clyburn, Shengelia, Youssoupha Fall o Juani Marcos, mientras Jan Vesely dice adiós al baloncesto profesional. Pocas veces el Palau había visto salir de golpe tanta experiencia, talento y galones, virtudes que ni siquiera atesoraban Myles Cale y Miles Norris, que salieron como llegaron, fundidos en la mediocridad. La catarsis es de las que hacen época. Si un aficionado azulgrana hubiese estado incomunicado en una isla desierta los dos últimos meses y al regresar le dicen que su equipo se ha reforzado con Olivier Nkamhoua, Tosan Evbuomwan, Agustín Ubal, Tyrese Martin, Justin Robinson, Stanley Umude... creería que le están gastando una broma. Ni el 'soci' más entusiasta daría crédito a tanto desconocido. Es el sello de su nuevo director deportivo, Xevi Pujol, especialista en descubrir talento antes que nadie, levantar plantillas altamente competitivas y exprimir al máximo presupuestos muy inferiores a los de sus rivales. Lo hizo con éxito antes en el Manresa y en el Baskonia. Pero el Barça es un morlaco de plaza de primera categoría. Y tanto 'sobresaliente' entraña un alto riesgo: "Hay un poco más de presión por tener muchos jugadores nuevos, el equipo necesitará más tiempo de lo normal por razones obvias, pero creo que tenemos talento y necesitamos trabajarlo para jugar como queremos", reconoce Sekulic. Es una apuesta arriesgada que sólo tienen dos salidas posibles: puerta grande o enfermería. Y el Barça lleva ya demasiadas cornadas en la última década. Kevin Punter, Juan Núñez, Joel Parra y Darío Brizuela, son junto al vetusto Palau Blaugrana (hasta que estrenen en 2029 nuevo pabellón) los cuatro únicos supervivientes de las cogidas de los últimos años en una plantilla que urgía rejuvenecer. Y Pujol lo ha conseguido. Las salidas tenían una media de 31,8 años y las llegadas promedian 26,1, casi 5,7 años menos. "Era una de las ideas del club, no solo mía. Queríamos tener un equipo más joven para cambiar un poco lo que pasó en las últimas temporadas", admitió Sekulic. La reconstrucción de Xevi Pujol empieza desde el timón. Justin Robinson aterriza tras firmar una notable irrupción en la Euroliga con el Paris Basketball, mientras Umoja Gibson llega con el aval de una brillante temporada en la EuroCup. Dos perfiles distintos para hacer olvidar el enorme vacío enorme que deja en la dirección del juego las marchas de Satoransky y Laprovittola. El lavado de cara también alcanza la pintura. Josh Nebo aporta músculo y contundencia bajo el aro, Olek Balcerowski regresa a la Liga Endesa, Olivier Nkamhoua aterriza tras explotar en Italia y Tosan Evbuomwan añade versatilidad en las posiciones interiores. A ellos se unen Agustín Ubal, Tyrese Martin y Stanley Umude para completar un grupo lleno de incógnitas, pero con mucha hambre y ganas de salir del anonimato general. El resultado es un Barça que ya no se parece en casi nada al Barça de hace apenas dos meses. La revolución, a falta de la incorporación de algún pívot más para reforzar la pintura, está hecha; ahora falta comprobar si también es la solución. Porque en el Palau ya no basta con competir: después de tantos cambios, solo ganar títulos volverá a devolverle al Barça la apariencia de siempre.

articles.title: Pistons Fan Favorite City Editions Returning for 2026-27 Season
articles.summary: The Pistons’ 2026-27 City Edition jerseys have leaked, and fans could see the return of the popular red uniforms from Cade Cunningham’s rookie season.
articles.body:
The Pistons City Edition jerseys have leaked for the 2026-27 season , and according to NBA Uniform Tracker , fans can expect the return of their 2021-22 city editions. This leak came in a thread reporting on each team's city-edition uniforms for this season. Red jerseys have always been part of the Pistons' lineage, and whenever they've gone away, fans have clamored for their return. These red uniforms, however, are special for numerous reasons.

For starters, these were the city edition jerseys during Pistons superstar Cade Cunningham's rookie year. In a season that didn't have much to celebrate in the win column, fans did have something to hang their hats on: the emergence of a franchise star. Having the chance to bring these uniforms back now that Cunningham has cemented himself as a first-team All-NBA caliber player on a team that just won 60 games is something lots of fans will be excited about.

In addition, these city editions felt more like a love letter to multiple eras of Pistons basketball than any other. Big Sean included numerous small details in the design, including the three championships being commemorated on the bottom of the jersey, lightning bolts down the sides of the shorts recognizing the Pistons of the late 70's, and multiple iterations of team logos of old (including, in this writer's opinion, the greatest logo in the history of basketball in the horse logo).

With all the different city editions introduced, and the risks being taken with other NBA uniforms this season , it makes sense to fall back on a classic. The intention of the city edition (besides another excuse from Nike to sell new jerseys) is to celebrate the city and the culture of each team. No other city edition has come close to capturing the hearts and wallets of Pistons fans. The red Cunningham jersey is still one of the most common to be seen around the concourse of Little Caesars Arena. Now that they are set to make their return, expect to see a sea of red amongst the LCA.

articles.title: Luka Doncic could finally get highest NBA individual award as he begins Lakers journey as a leader following Lebron James’ departure: "I think it's pretty well set up”
articles.summary: NBA News: Luka Doncic has spent years building an MVP resume without the hardware to show for it. That could change fast.With LeBron James gone and the Lakers n.
articles.body: Luka Doncic has spent years building an MVP resume without the hardware to show for it. That could change fast.With LeBron James gone and the Lakers now fully his team, Doncic walks into the 2026-27 season as the lone face of a franchise reshaping its identity around him. ESPN insider Tim MacMahon thinks the timing could not line up better for a first MVP trophy, and the numbers already back that theory up.NBA insider predicts Luka Doncic could earn MVP award in 2026-27 seasonMacMahon pointed out that the pressure on the Lakers is about as light as it has been since LeBron first arrived, which oddly works in Doncic's favor. Voters tend to reward players who outperform modest team expectations, and Doncic has the individual numbers to make that happen regardless of what the roster around him looks like.Last season, he averaged 33.5 points, 8.3 assists and 7.7 rebounds across 64 games as the Lakers finished 53-29. Even with those numbers, he finished fourth in MVP voting. MacMahon believes matching that production while keeping LA competitive changes the math entirely."I think it's pretty well set up for Luka to potentially win his first," MacMahon said, adding that a similar 53-win season paired with those kinds of stats would give Doncic what he called a serious case. "And a narrative where the expectations for the Lakers are as low as they've been since LeBron arrived."Doncic's scoring numbers adds to the MVP pushMVP isn't the only trophy in play. ESPN's Brian Windhorst joined MacMahon on The Hoop Collective Podcast to back Doncic as an early favorite for the scoring title too. He led the league at 33.5 points per game last season, marking the second time in three years he's topped the NBA in scoring, after averaging 33.9 points with Dallas in 2024-25.Stacking a scoring title on top of MVP buzz only strengthens the individual narrative. Doncic isn't just filling a stat sheet, he's doing it while carrying more organizational weight than at any point in his career.Health and history are the final pieces of the puzzleThe Lakers haven't had an MVP winner since Kobe Bryant took it home in 2007-08, and that drought hangs over this whole conversation. Doncic spent his offseason rehabbing a hamstring issue rather than chasing headlines, and he now enters camp fully healthy alongside Austin Reaves as the team's other veteran leader.Doncic has been this close before, finishing third in MVP voting back in 2023-24. What's different now is the setup around him. Stay on the floor, keep producing at his usual level, and push the Lakers past 50 wins again, and voters may finally run out of reasons to look elsewhere. articles.title: 76ers' Jaylen Brown Hypes LeBron James, Tyrese Maxey While Reacting to Workout Video
articles.summary: Jaylen Brown broke down a recent workout video that included him and new Philadelphia 76ers teammates LeBron James and Tyrese Maxey during his Twitch stream on Sunday.
articles.body:
Jaylen Brown broke down a recent workout video that included him and new Philadelphia 76ers teammates LeBron James and Tyrese Maxey during his Twitch stream on Sunday.

"Maxey is a dog. LeBron is... you don't even need to say what LeBron is," Brown noted. "He looked good, healthy. It's gonna be that. So we working, man. This is one of our first workouts. We worked out a few times. So that's good to just get in the gym with your teammates, get a feel for one another. Feel that the energy level is high, the talent is high. We've just got to come with the right approach. ... LeBron is in his Kobe year, year 24. And we in the birthplace of the Bean. Come on dog, the energy is there."

There is ample excitement in Philadelphia after the offseason additions of James and Brown, and for good reason—that duo, alongside Maxey, Joel Embiid and VJ Edgecombe has the ability to be the best starting lineup in basketball.

Much will depend on how quickly the group gels and settles into roles, of course, but the vibes are high in the City of Brotherly Love.

articles.title: Dallas Wings Teammate Heads To The Locker Room After Nasty Collision Involving Paige Bueckers
articles.summary: A scary moment briefly interrupted the Dallas Wings’ latest game in what should’ve been a routine outing against the Connecticut Sun. During the game, star P...
articles.body:
A scary moment briefly interrupted the Dallas Wings' latest game in what should've been a routine outing against the Connecticut Sun. During the game, star Paige Bueckers and a teammate collided, sparking injury concern for the Wings early.

During the first quarter, Paige Bueckers and Alanna Smith ran into each other, causing a nasty collision that left both hitting the floor. Wings reporter Myah Taylor explained what happened in a post on X.

"Alanna Smith and Paige Bueckers collided on the court," Taylor posted to X . "Bueckers is still in the game, but Smith walked off the court."

Indeed, Smith headed off the court and into the locker room, sparking worry among Wings fans online, as she seemingly injured her ankle.

However, good news soon followed. Taylor later reported that before the halftime break, Smith had returned to the bench and soon checked back into the game, getting back in form.

It was a solid outing from the forward, who played 17 minutes and logged seven points and two rebounds. Smith also put up a solid defensive effort on the Sun's forwards, holding Diamond Miller to just eight points on 2-14 shooting as well as 0-6 from three-point range.

Paige Bueckers, for her part, played well too, logging 15 points on 6-13 shooting, along with six assists and two rebounds, helping lead the team to a comfortable 97-71 win over the struggling Sun.

This isn't the first unfortunate collision that Paige Bueckers has been a part of this season. On July 20th, against the Los Angeles Sparks, Bueckers ran into Sparks center Nneka Ogwumike with 3:33 left in the fourth quarter. The sequence looked serious, as Bueckers hit her head on the floor and was taken out of the game.

For Smith, the injury came in the middle of a bounce-back stretch for the forward. After joining the Wings in a major free-agency move after a breakout 2025 season that saw her named the Co-Defensive Player of the Year alongside A'ja Wilson, she struggled to make an impact early in the season. She was replaced in the starting lineup just seven games into the season after a disastrous month of June.

"By the end of June, she had yet to post a double-digit scoring game, had more turnovers than assists, and recorded six blocks in 15 games," The IX Sports reporter Drake Keeler wrote in an August 19 report.

Through the first 21 games of her season, she averaged just 4.1 points and 3.0 rebounds per game on 40.5% from the field and 21.1% from three. However, since entering the month of August, she has completely turned her season around. Over 11 games this month, she has averaged 9.6 points, 5.8 rebounds, and 0.9 steals per game on 51.2% from the field and 32.3% from three.

Her improved play has also seen her return to the team's starting lineup, starting all 11 games that she has played in August.

In the middle of the improving stretch, Smith made it clear that she wanted to keep the upward trend going, refusing to put a "ceiling" on her play.

"I'd love to play better than what I'm playing right now," she told reporters postgame on August 12. "So hopefully it's onwards and upwards for not only myself, but the entire team too."

Dallas currently sits at 24-16, tied with the New York Liberty and the Washington Mystics in the standings, but holding the #8 seed due to tiebreaker rules. The team now hopes to stay solid after returning to play following the break for the FIBA World Cup, with their first game back set to be a showdown against the Los Angeles Sparks on 17 September.

Meanwhile, only time will tell if Smith can climb back to the heights that she reached during her time with the Minnesota Lynx, but if August is any indication, she has started to ramp up at the best time possible, with Paige Bueckers and Dallas set to appear in the playoffs for the first time in three seasons.

articles.title: ‘Nasty Work,’ ‘Not a Team Player’ — WNBA World Shreds Olivia Miles After Lynx Phenom’s 0-Assist Night vs. Angel Reese’s Dream
articles.summary: Olivia Miles-led Minnesota Lynx lost to Angel Reese’s Atlanta Dream 89-81 on Sunday, Aug. 30.
articles.body:
Olivia Miles-led Minnesota Lynx lost to Angel Reese's Atlanta Dream 89-81 on Sunday, Aug. 30. Miles finished with another 20+ scoring night. However, her zero assists put her under a microscope, attracting tons of reactions from the WNBA world.

Olivia Miles' 0-Assist Night Drew Harsh WNBA Reactions

Miles lit up the scoreboard with a team-high 21 points on 7-of-14 shooting and 6-of-7 from the charity stripe. But her playmaking was almost nonexistent, as she finished the game without a single assist. Besides, she also posted a team-worst minus-19 plus-minus during 30 minutes of play.

Her lack of involvement in creating opportunities for her teammates quickly became a major talking point, especially as the rookie phenom has been in MVP conversations.

"Stop telling me Olivia Miles deserves better odds for WNBA MVP than Caitlin Clark," OutKick's Jon Root asserted .

"Everybody on the Lynx roster got an assist today vs the Dream except for Olivia Miles… Nasty work," one WNBA observer highlighted .

For half of the game, Miles was even sloppy on the scoring end. During the first two quarters, she managed nine points.

X handle Letstalksports took a dig at Miles, calling her game "one-dimensional."

"Olivia Miles: 9 PTS, 0 AST — looking every bit like a rookie after struggling the last few games. Super one-dimensional right now. But y'all told me she's better than Caitlin Clark. SHUT THE HELL UP. 😭," Letstalksports joked .

Miles gained some momentum in the second half of the game and added 12 points to her tally. But her playmaking remained a no-show.

"Please stop mentioning Olivia Miles and Caitlin Clark in the same sentence. Immediately," Letstalksports iterated , highlighting Miles' stat line.

One X user took the criticism to another level, bringing Caitlin Clark into the picture and highlighting that the Indiana Fever superstar has never had a zero-assist night in her entire basketball career.

"Point guard Olivia Miles had zero assists today against the Dream and the worst plus-minus on her team. She needed to get her teammates involved in order to get the W, but couldn't do so. Fun fact: Caitlin Clark has never had a game in college or in the WNBA with no assists," the X user wrote .

"Olivia Miles leading the Lynx in scoring isn't a recipe for success. If she is not playmaking and getting the easy buckets for the others, the Lynx are an entirely different team, as we saw vs the Dream," another X user posted.

Miles played for Notre Dame and TCU during her collegiate career but never won the NCAA basketball championship. Her non-existent playmaking against the Dream also brought that fact into the spotlight.

"When your team goes on a run because you are not playing your role (pg with 0 assists), more obsessed with your own points, and a CONE on defense – you are not a team player nor a winner. This is why Olivia Miles never won a tournament in 4 years of college."

But the most glaring part of Miles' play during the night was her plus-minus score. Despite being the leading scorer, the Lynx rookie registered the worst minus-19 plus-minus, which highlights how ineffective her performance was against the Dream.

Putting that into perspective, one X user quipped , "Is that -19?"

Miles has been a steady presence for the Lynx throughout the season. She leads the team in both scoring and assists and has played a major role in the Lynx's 31-9 record and their position atop the WNBA standings.

But the Lynx have now dropped two straight games. With the playoffs approaching, a dip in Miles' playmaking could become a major concern for Minnesota.

articles.title: Angel Reese exchanges heated on-court moment with Lynx veteran during historic WNBA win
articles.summary: Angel Reese made WNBA history in the Atlanta Dream’s 89-81 win over the Minnesota Lynx, but also got into it with one of her opponents. Reese’s 15 points and...
articles.body:
Angel Reese made WNBA history in the Atlanta Dream's 89-81 win over the Minnesota Lynx, but also got into it with one of her opponents.

Reese's 15 points and 11 rebounds in this win led to her 29th double-double of the season, the most in a single season in WNBA history.

However, the focus wasn't completely on her historic stats, but it was also on a heated second-quarter exchange she had with Lynx's Courtney Williams.

Angel Reese clashes with Lynx's Courtney Williams

With under six minutes left in the second quarter, Reese got tangled up with Williams after a Lynx baseline double-team. The pair had to be separated, with some lip-reading fans claiming that Reese mocked Williams for being bald as they went their separate ways.

Reese has previously embraced her role as one of the Dream's on-court enforcers, so she was not going to let Williams get physical with her without facing the consequences of a slight tussle.

Both players went on with their performances, as Reese ended the night making history with her double-double, while also adding two assists, two steals, and a block.

Williams watched her Lynx fail to adequately neutralise the feisty Dream, as Courtney ended the game with 11 points (5-12 FG), three rebounds, four assists, and three steals.

Angel Reese's dream first season with Atlanta Dream

Reese is averaging 16.1 points and 12.4 rebounds this season, her first with the Dream after the Chicago Sky decided to trade her after just two seasons.

Players with Reese's potential often become cornerstone players for franchises, and the Dream will get that opportunity instead of the Sky after this acquisition.

It does not seem like Reese will ever be an offensive No. 1 option for a championship team, but a squad like the Dream, which has the players to do what she struggles at, is perfect for her future success.

She will be playing in the postseason, with the Dream's most likely first-round matchup right now looking like Caitlin Clark's Indiana Fever.

A dream debut season would definitely include beating Clark's Fever and then making as deep a run as possible in the remaining rounds to establish their status as future contenders.

articles.title: España ya tiene a sus 12 para el Mundial Femenino
articles.standfirst: El seleccionador Miguel Méndez da la lista definitiva con cinco jugadoras de la WNBA
articles.summary: El seleccionador Miguel Méndez da la lista definitiva con cinco jugadoras de la WNBA
articles.body: La Federación Española de Baloncesto ha anunciado la lista de 12 jugadoras que compondrán el equipo que participará en el Mundial Femenino que se disputará en Berlín desde el 4 hasta el 13 de septiembre. Tras una concentración compleja debido a la ausencia de las internacionales que estaban participando en la WNBA, el seleccionador Miguel Méndez ha hecho los descartes finales después del último amistoso, disputado este domingo ante China. Las 12 jugadoras seleccionadas son: Alba Torrens, María Conde, Paula Ginzo, Maite Cazorla, Raquel Carrera, Mariona Ortiz, Helena Pueyo, Iyana Martín, Awa Fam, Elena Buenavida, Megan Gustafson y Alicia Flórez. De todas ellas, sólo la capitana Torrens tiene experiencia mundialista. Ha disputado tres torneos con sendas medallas: plata en 2014 y bronce en 2010 y 2018. Después de los descartes de Txell Alarcón y Carolina Guerrero hace un par de semanas, al seleccionador le ha costado mucho hacer los últimos, que han sido Andrea Vilaró, Irati Etxarri, María Araújo, Aina Ayuso, Lola Pendande, Nerea Hermosa y Marta García. “Hemos pasado un día tenso, el de hacer el equipo definitivo. Ha sido especialmente difícil por el nivel de todas las jugadoras que han estado aquí. La gente no se imagina las vueltas que le hemos dado", asegura el técnico. Méndez considera que "dentro de las posibles estructuras de equipo, hemos elegido la que mejor nos va a representar en un Mundial" y mostraba su agradecimiento "a todas las jugadoras por el compromiso que han mostrado, especialmente este año, que es nuevo para todos. Hemos intentado hacerlo de la mejor manera posible y ha estado muy bien gracias, sobre todo, a su talante y profesionalidad”. España se presentará en el Mundial invicta en su preparación tras ganar los cinco amistosos más otro a puerta cerrada, pero ha sido una preparación de gran complejidad debido a la ausencia de las internacionales que militan en la WNBA. Awa Fam y María Conde se incorporaron a finales de la semana pasada, pudiendo ejercitarse ya con el grupo e incluso participar en el último de los partidos de preparación, disputado este domingo ante China. Raquel Carrera y Alicia Flórez se han sumado al grupo a su llegada a Madrid, donde este lunes tendrá lugar un acto despedida antes de viajar este martes a Berlín. En la capital alemana se añadirá la nacionalizada Megan Gustafson, que volará directamente desde Estados Unidos. España compartirá grupo con Alemania, Mali y Japón. Este viernes (17.45 horas) debutará ante la selección anfitriona en el encuentro más complicado de la primera fase. Durante la preparación ya le vencieron en un duelo a puerta cerrada. Este sábado, sin apenas descanso (11.30 horas) se medirá al combinado africano, al que recientemente barrió en otro de los amistosos. Para acabar, se las verá a Japón el lunes 7 (17.50 horas). Si la selección acaba primera y, como es previsible, Estados Unidos también, irían por el mismo lado del cuadro y podrían encontrarse en semifinales. El líder pasará directamente a cuartos de final evitando una peligrosa repesca de octavos en la que cada segundo de grupo se medirá a un tercero. En ese caso, España tendría que enfrentarse a Hungría, Corea del Sur, Nigeria o Francia, aunque las galas apuntan a ser primeras.

articles.summary: La leyenda del baloncesto español, que este domingo cumplió 37 años, capitaneará a la selección femenina en el Mundial
articles.body: El día después de cumplir 37 años, Alba Torrens fue incluida en la lista de la selección femenina para el Mundial que se celebrará en Berlín desde este viernes y hasta el 13 de septiembre. "La ilusión por seguir se mantiene y se renueva", asegura quien es ya la sexta jugadora con más internacionalidades: 225. La alero capitaneará un grupo en el que es la única de las 12 internacionales con experiencia en la cita mundialista. De hecho atesora tres medallas en el campeonato: plata en 2014 y bronces en 2010 y 2018. Son sólo una parte de la cosecha de éxitos que ha recogido durante su dilatada carrera con la selección, que incluye 10 podios: también plata en los Juegos de 2016, oros en los Eurobasket de 2013 y 2017, platas en 2023 y 2025 y bronces en 2009 y 2015. Un palmarés que equivale a leyenda y a experiencia. Eso y una calidad aún intacta le han hecho un hueco en el equipo que irá al Mundial. Porque su figura tiene una enorme importancia en un vestuario muy joven y porque, además, aún conserva su amenaza ofensiva como ha demostrado en la preparación, a la que ha llegado bien físicamente, y durante la temporada. En su regreso a casa, a Mallorca, ha sido una pieza importante en el ascenso a la Liga Femenina Endesa del Azulmarino, que disputó la Liga Femenina Challenge, segunda categoría del baloncesto femenino español. Tras ese éxito, confía en sumar otro con la selección en el Mundial.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese must now work together at Women's World Cup as WNBA takes a high-stakes break
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese must unite as teammates in Berlin as the U.S. defends a 30-game win streak at the Women's Basketball World Cup.
articles.body: The U.S. is headed to a battle in Berlin. Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese will have to work together to uphold American dominance in the Women's Basketball World Cup in September. At home, the WNBA will take a two-week break from hosting the chaos of the 2026 season. So Americans will have to root together for their biggest stars on the world stage. The U.S. has won four consecutive World Cups in a row and this year's team will also have to protect an active 30-game win streak. What happens in Berlin could very well shape the climate of the league that the players return to when the WNBA season resumes. Can Clark and Reese work together? Clark and Reese have spent more than three years framed as adversaries. The last time they were on a basketball court, Clark was seen laughing as she walked by Reese, who had just missed the game-winning layup. Their rivalry fueled the 2023 national championship game between Iowa and LSU. It followed them into a rematch in the 2024 NCAA Tournament, then into the WNBA as the top two contenders for Rookie of the Year. Every matchup, foul and postgame comment became another invitation for fans to choose a side. But at times, they've also shown glimpses of what that can look like when playing together. Reese first said, "one day, hopefully, we can be teammates," while discussing Clark in an October 2024 Wall Street Journal article. They first became teammates at the 2024 WNBA All-Star Game, when Clark recorded 10 assists and Reese finished with 12 points and 11 rebounds in Team WNBA’s victory over the U.S. Olympic team. CAITLIN CLARK HELPS WNBA SHATTER ANOTHER TV RATINGS RECORD AS FEVER-DREAM DRAWS MASSIVE AUDIENCE In March, Clark and Reese helped the U.S. go 5-0 at the World Cup qualifying tournament in Puerto Rico. There was an awkward moment when Clark appeared to ignore a high five invitation from Reese during one of the games. Clark earned tournament MVP honors after averaging 11.6 points and a tournament-leading 6.4 assists. Reese averaged a team-high eight rebounds while shooting 52.2% from the field. "Team chemistry is everything," Reese said during the qualifying tournament. "Some of us have played with each other on our respective teams, but we have to come together and find your role. Everybody’s not going to be able to do everything that they do on their respective team." Clark and Reese will play alongside established champions A’ja Wilson, Breanna Stewart, Napheesa Collier and Chelsea Gray in Berlin. What will happen during the national anthems? The available rules and national-team precedent point to the entire U.S. team standing on the court for "The Star-Spangled Banner" in Berlin. Whether every player places her hand over her heart or sings along is a separate question that neither USA Basketball nor FIBA rules answer. The issue has drawn new attention during the 2026 WNBA season because teams have followed different routines. Several WNBA teams historically and routinely remain in the locker room or clear the floor during the playing of the national anthem as part of pregame routines. CHINA’S INFLUENCE MACHINE: FEDERAL RECORDS EXPOSE BEIJING’S PUSH TO SWAY AMERICA The Atlanta Dream remained in their locker room while the anthem played before their Aug. 16 game against the Indiana Fever. That left Reese and Rhyne Howard, both members of the World Cup roster, off the court while Clark, Aliyah Boston and the rest of the Fever stood along the sideline. Clark stood facing the flag with her hands behind her back. Sophie Cunningham placed her right hand over her heart. The difference generated criticism of Clark online, although nothing in the WNBA rulebook requires players to sing or place a hand over their heart. The rules change when those players leave their WNBA teams and join the national program. USA Basketball’s code of conduct requires participants to follow FIBA and USA Basketball rules, attend team functions as directed and "demonstrate proper respect during the playing of the national anthem." The code does not define "proper respect," but it gives USA Basketball authority to investigate alleged violations and impose discipline. FIBA also controls the ceremonies in Berlin. Its 2026 regulations state that only anthems and flags of countries or national federations recognized by FIBA may be used. The regulations leave the details of World Cup ceremonies to the tournament’s hosting documents. They do not publicly prescribe whether a player must sing, place a hand over her heart or assume another specific posture. FIBA’s code of conduct additionally prohibits players and other "basketball parties" from using gestures, words or objects to transmit political or ideological messages that are deemed unfit for a sporting event. The rule does not specifically identify kneeling, remaining silent or declining to place a hand over the heart as violations. It does, however, give FIBA greater control over demonstrations than the WNBA has exercised during its domestic season. Past U.S. teams have treated international competition differently from the WNBA. American players who routinely remained off the court during WNBA anthems stood together for them at the 2021 Tokyo Olympics. Sue Bird, then the team’s captain and now the managing director who selected the 2026 roster, said wearing a USA uniform changed the context. "You are wearing USA jerseys and it does change the conversation a little bit and what you’re representing," Bird said at the time. "With that, I don’t feel like a hypocrite in any way. Everyone knows where we stand. I don’t think it contradicts anything since we’re actually doing the work." The U.S. players stood with their arms linked during that Olympic run. There also were no reported anthem protests during the United States’ five-game World Cup qualifying run in Puerto Rico in March. That team included Clark, Reese, Howard, Paige Bueckers and Kahleah Copper. As of Aug. 30, no member of the World Cup roster has publicly announced plans to kneel, leave the floor or conduct another demonstration during the anthem in Berlin. Rival world powers collide The Americans will open the World Cup against China on Sept. 4. It will be a rematch of the 2022 World Cup final. Women's basketball dominance over America's greatest current geopolitical rival will be on the line. There have been 15 World Cup and Olympic meetings between the countries, and the U.S. has won all 15. Two of those victories came at the 2022 World Cup. The U.S. beat China 77-63 during group play and then defeated it again, 83-61, in the final. The victory gave the Americans their fourth consecutive world championship. The government agency called the silver medal "a perfect birthday gift to the country," according to China Daily. What happens during national anthems will also be a point of potential contrast during the game against China. China has had a national anthem law since 2017. The law specifically lists major sporting events as occasions for the anthem and directs those present to stand solemnly and behave respectfully. Deliberately insulting the anthem in public can result in detention or criminal prosecution under Chinese law. The law will not govern what the American players do in Berlin. But it shows how differently the two countries can treat displays of patriotism at sporting events. articles.title: The Best NBA Player at Every Age Right Now
articles.summary: The last few years have given us plenty of discussion on where the NBA might turn for a face of the league when LeBron James and Stephen Curry retire.
articles.body:
The last few years have given us plenty of discussion on where the NBA might turn for a face of the league when LeBron James and Stephen Curry retire.

But they've also seen an influx in massive new talents who look ready to take the mantle whenever it's vacated.

You'll see plenty below, as we look at the best players at each and every age* from 19 through 41.

And just to be clear, we're using player ages as of the day of publication (rather than their season age, which is where they are on February 1).

While the choice at each age will rely heavily on basic and advanced numbers from past performance, the idea is to pick who will be the best player in every group this season. That requires plenty of subjectivity.

You'll also see references to other contenders throughout the slideshow. And while that generally means there's some universe in which those players could end up on top, some are longer shots than others.

*There are no current players at age 39.

If we were going with season age, Cooper Flagg would be among the 20-year-olds, but he doesn't hit that mark until December. That means he'll play a significant chunk of his second season as a teenager.

And though the incoming rookie class includes several potential superstars (like the contenders listed below), Flagg's year of experience will give him a meaningful cushion between himself and the rest of the 19-year-olds.

His developmental arrow is already darn-near vertical.

As a rookie, he averaged 18.8 points and 4.1 assists in his first 43 games. And from that point to the end of the campaign, he was at 24.7 points and 5.1 assists.

Flagg may have to cede some touches to Kyrie Irving this season, but his return will also divert some defensive attention away from him too. And that could help Flagg maintain the kind of production he had at the end of 2025-26.

As promising as the trio below is, they won't consistently reach those heights as rookies.

Contenders: Cameron Boozer, Darryn Peterson, AJ Dybantsa

Flagg got some seasoning in the regular season that the rest of the 19-year-olds didn't, but Dylan Harper wound up with an even better crash course.

As a rookie, he was a key contributor to the San Antonio Spurs' unexpected NBA Finals run. And that gave him an experience boost that almost no 20-year-old can boast.

In 23 playoff games, Harper averaged 14.1 points and 2.7 assists in just 26.7 minutes. He trailed only Victor Wembanyama and Julian Champagnie among Spurs rotation players in playoff box plus/minus. And in the Finals, his scoring average climbed to 18.0 points in 31.0 minutes.

Even in the highest-pressure moments, Harper looked poised. He manipulated defenders off the dribble like a 10-year vet. He wasn't shy about taking big shots. For long stretches, he looked like the obvious Robin to Wemby's Batman.

Harper isn't just the best 20-year-old in the NBA right now. He has a chance to be an All-Star and one of the best guards at any age in 2026-27.

Kon Knueppel wasn't just one of the best shooters in the NBA last season. According to various catch-all metrics from around the internet, he was around a top-40(ish) player.

Now, a lot of that impact was driven by the shooting, for sure. He was third in the league in threes per game at 3.4. And there were only two qualified non-bigs with better effective field-goal percentages. But his game extends beyond that foundation.

Knueppel has solid playmaking and pick-and-roll instincts for a wing. He's probably not a plus defender yet, but he's also not a disaster.

And if he makes even marginal improvements in those areas while maintaining the shooting, he could be a borderline All-Star as early as this season.

Contenders: Stephon Castle, VJ Edgecombe, Collin Murray-Boyles

Fat Joe Hypes MJ, LeBron as GOATs on New Album

This is the most obvious call of the exercise so far. The "contenders" below are really only listed for the sake of consistency.

Victor Wembanyama is far and away the best 22-year-old in the league. He might even be its MVP at this point next year.

After averaging 25.0 points, 11.5 rebounds, 3.1 blocks and 3.1 assists, Wemby became the first unanimous Defensive Player of the Year in league history and took his way-ahead-of-schedule San Antonio Spurs to the NBA Finals.

He's the kind of rim protector who can be a defense unto himself. And he's developed into a high-impact offensive player far quicker than he had any right to.

Contenders: Keyonte George, Cason Wallace, Reed Sheppard (but really no one)

There's a real debate to be had between Amen Thompson and Paolo Banchero for this spot.

Banchero certainly scores at higher volume. And though he's yet to come anywhere near a league- average effective field-goal percentage, his outside shot commands more respect from opposing defenses.

But his advantages over Thompson may end there.

Amen is already one of the best and most dynamic perimeter defenders in the NBA. Relative to his size and position, he's at least as good a rebounder. He's a more self-aware offensive player (hence, his superior scoring efficiency). And despite having fewer opportunities to isolate or run pick-and-roll , Thompson had about the same assist rate as Banchero.

Even if Amen's jumper never becomes a real weapon, he probably checks enough other boxes to warrant this selection. If the shot does come along, he could become a perennial All-Star.

Contenders: Paolo Banchero, Brandon Miller, Ausar Thompson

This is where the decision to use current age instead of season age becomes a little dicey, because Cade Cunningham turns 25 in September, around a month before the regular season starts.

But as you'll see in a moment, the next category is already loaded. So, we'll take this opportunity to squeeze Cade in with the 24-year-olds while we can.

And though there are good arguments for Alperen Şengün (with his point center skills), Jalen Johnson (with his point forward skills) and Chet Holmgren (with his defensive impact), none of them are quite as far along as Cade.

Cunningham, like Banchero, has struggled with scoring efficiency throughout his career, but he more than makes up for it with his volume playmaking.

Over the last two seasons, Cunningham has averaged 9.5 assists. And he finished top seven in MVP voting in both of those campaigns.

Regardless of whether his jump shot is falling, Cade's ability to engineer individual offensive possessions has quickly made him among the best creators in the NBA.

And one thing we've learned in recent seasons is that scoring from an individual player is nice, but it's even better to have someone capable of being an engine. Cunningham is an engine.

Contenders: Alperen Şengün, Jalen Johnson, Chet Holmgren

As promised, this group is jam-packed with talent. And while some of the "contenders" listed throughout this slideshow may only be here nominally, there are worlds in which anyone below could emerge as the best of this bunch.

But for now, Anthony Edwards feels like a pretty safe call.

When he was the No. 1 overall pick in 2020, he looked like a freak athlete who might achieve superstardom if he just became an average jump shooter.

Six years later, he still has the bounce, and that jumper has become far more dangerous than even the most optimistic fans could've imagined. Over the last two seasons, Edwards has averaged 28.1 points and hit 39.6 percent of a whopping 9.5 three-point attempts per game.

He's quickly developed into one of the best scorers the NBA has ever seen (he's top 20 all time in career playoff scoring average). And there's still some room to grow as a playmaker and defender.

Contenders: Tyrese Maxey, Scottie Barnes, LaMelo Ball, Evan Mobley, Jalen Williams, Deni Avdija, Franz Wagner

Last time we saw Tyrese Haliburton in action, he had his underdog Indiana Pacers leading Game 7 of the NBA Finals on the road.

And though one of the most devastating injuries in sports ended his pursuit of the title, there's reason to believe Haliburton will have his Pacers right back in the hunt.

Even if the ruptured Achilles took a hint of his athleticism away, Haliburton's craft, vision and passing ability should be every bit as dangerous as it was pre-injury. Those were more important ingredients for his production than athleticism anyway.

And that production has been pretty absurd since he joined the Pacers. In his three full seasons in Indiana, Haliburton has averaged 10.2 assists, 2.9 threes and 2.1 turnovers, while shooting 38.3 percent from deep.

Contenders: Zion Williamson, Darius Garland, Jaren Jackson Jr.

This is another one where there's really no debate, unless Trae Young or (even less likely) Ja Morant has an epic resurgence with a new team in 2026-27. Even then, it'd be tough for either to reach the heights where Luka Dončić consistently operates.

Luka is, without question, one of the best and most prolific offensive engines the NBA has ever produced. He's won two of the last three scoring titles. He's averaged at least 30 points in three of the last four seasons. In that four-year stretch, he's put up 32.2 points, 8.5 rebounds, 8.5 assists and 3.6 threes, with an above- average three-point percentage.

And now that LeBron James has moved on to the Philadelphia 76ers, the Los Angeles Lakers might need even more from Luka in 2026-27.

Even with Austin Reaves still around, Luka's shooting and pick-and-roll volume could tick up a bit. And if the Lakers finish in the top three or four of the West, there will be a very real push for Dončić's first MVP.

Contenders: Trae Young, Ja Morant (but really no one)

The "but really no one" tag below may feel a little disrespectful to four-time First Team All-NBA forward Jayson Tatum, but he's coming off a ruptured Achilles and never quite hit the MVP level Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's played at the last two years.

And considering the fact that SGA just had his 28th birthday this summer, there's no reason to expect any kind of step back in 2026-27.

He's right in the middle of his prime, has averaged at least 30 points in each of his last four campaigns and scored with almost Nikola Jokić-like efficiency in 2025-26.

With his ability to control pace, consistently get to his spots, draw shooting fouls and knock down shots from all three levels, SGA figures to be one of the most dominant offensive players in the NBA again this season.

Contenders: Jayson Tatum, Michael Porter Jr., Austin Reaves (but really no one)

It feels like Donovan Mitchell's stint with the Cleveland Cavaliers has been nitpicked as much as it's been celebrated. For NBA players, analysis often degrades to little more than "what have you done for me lately?", even for those with championships.

When you're like Mitchell, and you don't have the title, that line of thinking is harder to shake.

But Mitchell, despite standing just 6'2" as a shooting guard, has made the All-Star team in each of his last seven campaigns. He's finished top seven in MVP voting in three of his four Cleveland campaigns. And as a Cav, he's put up 26.7 points, 5.3 assists and 3.3 threes.

Mitchell is one of the most consistently productive combo guards in the NBA and will once again headline one of the league's best starting lineups in 2026-27.

Contenders: Jamal Murray, Bam Adebayo, Jaylen Brown, Devin Booker

Undoubtedly one of the best playoff guards in NBA history, Jalen Brunson just stamped his legacy with an NBA championship and Finals MVP in June.

The most recent run brought his career postseason numbers up to 26.0 points ( 17th all time), 5.5 assists and 2.4 threes. And since he's been with the Knicks, his teams' playoff net rating is 4.1 points better when he's on the floor.

After being drafted in the second round and previously cast as a career backup, Brunson has improbably developed into one of the best scorers in the league, a master manipulator out of the pick-and-roll and one of the most clutch offensive players ever.

Contenders: Karl-Anthony Towns, Domantas Sabonis

Nikola Jokić has finished top two in MVP voting in each of the last six seasons, a feat only matched by Larry Bird and Bill Russell.

And though Giannis Antetokounmpo may find some new life in his first season with the Miami Heat, the gap between him and Jokić on offense may be too big to overcome.

Jokić has legitimate arguments to be considered both a top-five passer of all time and one of the 5-10 best we've ever seen in terms of shooting touch in and around the paint.

Those things combined with his offensive feel make him one of the absolute best engines the league has ever seen and a likely contender for his fourth MVP.

If Joel Embiid can stay even remotely healthy, this group is almost certainly his in a runaway. Of course, at his age and with his injury history, it's not likely he'll play anywhere near enough games to qualify for individual awards.

Still, when he is available, and in lineups where defenders have to be aware of Tyrese Maxey, Jaylen Brown, VJ Edgecombe and LeBron James, Embiid is going to feast on the offensive end.

Over the last two years, Embiid has appeared in a total of 57 games, but he's averaged 25.8 points in 31.1 minutes.

Few things in the league are as reliable as Embiid's elbow jumpers after a jab step or two. And with so many weapons around him, his assist numbers could tick up too.

Contenders: Derrick White, Pascal Siakam

Another perennial injury risk, Anthony Davis is almost like a more defensive-minded version of Embiid.

He doesn't drive offense in quite the same way, but he's also a far more effective and impactful defender.

But again, he comes with a bright, flashing "when available" qualifier.

Assuming he can play 50-plus games, and considering the fact he'll likely share the floor with Trae Young, Davis is still talented enough to average around 25 and 10, while anchoring a defense.

Like Haliburton, Kyrie Irving is coming back after missing all of 2025-26. But unlike Haliburton, he's doing so well into his 30s.

At Kyrie's age, bouncing back from something like a torn ACL comes with a lot less predictability. A slightly slower first step could have a significant impact on his game.

But Kyrie also relies pretty heavily on his high-end offensive skills. The ball-handling and jump shot certainly haven't abandoned him. And he should be pretty motivated to prove those are still there with a chance to enter free agency next season.

Even as he approaches his late 30s, Kawhi Leonard remains one of the absolute best wing/forwards in the NBA.

Last season, he averaged a career-high 27.9 points, to go along with 3.6 assists and 1.9 steals (his highest mark since 2017-18).

He's not the total lockdown defender he was in his prime, but he's still a clear plus on that end too.

At some point, age and injuries are going to catch up enough to slow him to the point it shows up in the numbers. That might even happen this season. But there's truly no one else even close to him among the league's 35-year-olds.

It may feel unfair to Damian Lillard not to give him the same benefit of the doubt given to Haliburton and Irving, but coming back from a ruptured Achilles at 36 is a monumental feat.

And though he may still be more impactful than Jrue Holiday on the offensive end, Holiday still being a clear plus on the defensive end gives him a slight edge overall.

Last season, Holiday helped the Portland Trail Blazers get back to the playoffs, averaged 16.3 points and 6.1 assists in 29.4 minutes and shot 37.8 percent from deep.

Contenders: Damian Lillard, Paul George, Draymond Green

Like Cunningham, Kevin Durant is sneaking in just before the buzzer here. He turns 38 in September, but our (admittedly arbitrary) rules have him among the 37-year-olds for this exercise.

And though James Harden (who just turned 37 this month) is still one of the best creators and distributors in the NBA, Kevin Durant's size and pure scoring are still enough to put him over the top.

Last season, KD averaged 26.0 points with a 64.1 true shooting percentage. Jokić, SGA and Giannis were the only other players in the league who matched or exceeded both marks.

Even as Stephen Curry ages well into his late 30s, he's still among the very most dangerous and defense-altering offensive players in the NBA.

His instincts and relentlessness as an off-ball mover drags opponents all over the floor. That creates or widens openings for his teammates and is still the most important ingredient in the Golden State Warriors' attack.

And of course, plenty of that movement still results in catch-and-shoot opportunities. And Curry remains one of the most dynamic players in the world on that front.

Last season, he put up 26.6 points and 4.4 threes, while shooting 39.3 percent from deep.

Al Horford's numbers don't leap off the screen, but his experience, shooting and passing should still make him a useful bench player as he enters his age-40 season.

In his first season with the Golden State Warriors, Horford put up 8.3 points, 4.9 rebounds, 2.6 assists and 1.1 blocks in 21.5 minutes, while shooting 36.1 percent from deep.

And even if he's a little slower than he was last season, the Warriors are almost certainly going to need him to play some real minutes again in 2026-27.

As he nears his 42nd birthday in December, LeBron James is already the NBA's all-time leader in points, assists and steals logged at the age of 41. By the time December 30 rolls around, he'll likely top that list in rebounds too.

LeBron isn't just the best 41-plus player in the NBA right now. He's the best we've ever seen.

And every game he plays at this age and beyond only adds to his strongest argument in the GOAT debate with Michael Jordan: his unbelievable longevity.

LeBron obviously isn't quite the athlete he was in his prime, but he's made up for a lot of that loss of pop with an increase in wisdom.

And just last season, in his age-41 campaign and coming off a bout with sciatica, he averaged 20.9 points, 7.2 assists and 6.1 rebounds.

articles.title: Ranking Every WNBA Team's Best Jersey for the 2026 Season
articles.summary: This WNBA season has given us plenty to love so far.
articles.body:
This WNBA season has given us plenty to love so far.

We got two new expansion teams with the Toronto Tempo and the Portland Fire joining the league. We're currently being treated to one heck of a final stretch as a slew of teams claw their way around the playoff bubble.

We also got at least one new jersey from each team with the release of the 2026 Rebel Editions. There were many upgrades, a few head-scratchers and some major overall changes for teams around the league.

While we enjoy the playoff race on the court, let's take stock of the state of uniforms around the league. Each team has at least three jerseys in the current rotation: A white Heroine Edition, a bolder colored Explorer Edition and a third Rebel Edition meant to bring in some creativity and local influences. The Sparks, Liberty and Mercury have a fourth Court Origins jersey this year to celebrate the league's 30th season.

Let's rank 'em all. First, we'll pick the best jersey out of each team's collection, then we will pit that jersey against every other team's best jersey. So this is a best of the best jerseys, not a ranking of full sets.

Spoiler alert: The Storm's Heroine Edition was the only Heroine Edition jersey to make this list, and it's clearly at the bottom.

That's not a knock on the Heroine style. The simplicity of the classic whites establishes jersey consistency within the league, and it's a timeless and necessary part of any jersey collection. That is a knock on the Seattle Storm's 2026 Rebel and Explorer jerseys, which are anything but timeless or necessary.

Look, the yellow and green thing stands out. We appreciate a risk and a color scheme synonymous with one team, but it works better accented on a white jersey as opposed to a giant petri dish.

Please don't even start when it comes to the highlighter green Rebels. The Storm's color palette can only be described as "germ," and it's just too much. Achoo!

The Sky first introduced the fun "Skytown" logo as a reference to their "Chitown" home with their 2024 Rebels, and at the time we awarded them with the best jersey collection in the league partially due to the play on words.

To be fair, the ranking system was a bit different two seasons ago: We took the average of all three jerseys of each team, while today we are ranking by the best jersey in each team's collection.

The Sky's jersey collection as a whole is a cohesive, harmless trio, and the Skytown addition was a big jump from their previous third. There's no egregiously bad jersey in there, but nothing stands out. Today's rankings are more forgiving of a dud and emphasize the best singular jersey in each collection.

Still, it's a testament to the growth, innovation, and momentum of the WNBA that the Sky went from first to almost worst in two short seasons. We still like the concept of "Skytown," but other teams' Rebel jerseys got better, while the Sky's got slightly worse.

The change from the milky white and blue color scheme to a solid blue is boring. Now, the black pinstripe jersey from the Explorer Edition is the best in Chicago's set, and that could use an upgrade while we're at it.

We'll be honest, we are absolutely docking the Mercury because all four (4!) of their current jerseys are worse than their former gradient-style Explorer Editions. You had a slam dunk, you have the perfect team and color scheme for a tasteful gradient moment, and you took that magic away from us?

We cannot forgive the Mercury for their decisions, even if their collection as a whole is still pretty solid. Their Court Origins edition is basically the exact replica of their original jersey, and that is what it is.

The current Rebel is the closest we've got to the beloved gradient of yore, so we'll begrudgingly allow it.

Angel Reese breaks yet another WNBA record

The Tempo are here, and they've come bearing sponsors!

At first, we loved their Rebel Edition: Most notably, the speedy T on the Tempo wordmark. We understand—especially in a team's first year—that sponsors keep this thing running. We expect the highs and lows of expansion teams and their first uniforms. Still, the CIBC branding looming larger than the actual Tempo logo on the Rebel Editions is an egregious party foul.

The ad branding is less offensive on the Explorer Edition, and we're partial to burgundy.

There are whispers of Atlanta everywhere throughout this jersey. The lowercase and rounded font of the "atl" heading is clean. The Georgia Peach combined with the big "A" is cute and fun. The peach-colored accents are subtle enough to work surprisingly well with the black and blue color scheme.

This is what the Rebel Editions are all about, and best of all? The sponsor ad is tiny and well-placed.

Let's be real: Would any current Aces jersey move the needle if the team weren't a dynasty? Probably not. Should Nike send A'ja Wilson a bouquet of flowers at least weekly to thank her for the countless iconic moments that have brainwashed us basketball fans into a favorable opinion of these generally bland jerseys? Probably!

Regardless, the Aces did well with their Rebel Edition, and we can't deny the satisfaction of a black, white, and red jersey for Sin City, even if they tend to stick to the script.

The Rebel Edition is also a more entertaining departure from the standard silver, white, and black for the Aces. The font is impeccable and fun without being too cutesy. The nod to the UNLV Runnin' Rebels is undeniable.

The sponsor ad is a little distracting, but less of an eyesore than some others on the list. This jersey is fine-to-good, and we get why a dynasty opts for simplicity, but we'd perhaps like to see something just for funsies from the all-business Aces at some point.

Minnesota's uniforms could never top our uniform lists due to, say it with us, the neon green of it all. Even a speck of that putrid color is going to dock you a bit. The Lynx, at least, incorporate it rather inoffensively.

The lake blue primary color is gorgeous, and somewhat rare in the land of sports uniforms. The Timberwolves and the Lynx did a great job claiming lake blue for the land of 10,000 lakes. The cohesiveness between the two teams, the representation of their state, and the gorgeous color itself almost makes us want to forgive them for the highlighter green of it all.

It's difficult to rank the jersey of a relocating team during its last season in the league. We've appreciated the nods the Connecticut Sun uniforms have given to the Mohegan Tribe over the years, although months of conflict between the WNBA and the tribe leading up to the sale of the team complicates and bittersweetens the gesture.

Business decisions and their fallout aside, the pop of orange the Sun gave this league will be missed. These Explorer Editions also feature the best trim of any WNBA jersey, and it's a pattern formed by Mohegan symbols.

We will miss the uniqueness of this trim.

We love a jersey that jumps out at you before you go seeking it out. That's the 2026 Mystics Rebel Edition, and it's screaming "funky!" "aura!" at us before we even slow down to think.

When we do collect our thoughts, we realize this is extremely different than a typical Mystics jersey. The purple gradient is gorgeous, as is the cursive "District," and the subtle "of change" underneath, but there's more to it.

The jersey pays homage to D.C.'s U Street, the Black Broadway era of the 1920s-'50s, and the many Black women who kept the area running through times of success and of hardship. Read all about it here .

There's nothing better than a Rebel Edition with an awesome backstory and an aesthetically pleasing jersey to match. The Mystics executed that well, here.

When these were released, we immediately exhaled at the sight of seafoam green. Don't mess with what works, don't mess with what makes you, you. The Lady Liberty seafoam green is synonymous with the New York Libs, and it doesn't hurt that it's a gorgeous and fun color.

We do have to accept the reality that jerseys are going to have ads in our year of the Lord 2026, so it at least gave us a tongue-in-cheek chuckle that Liberty Mutual is the sponsorship patch on this one.

5. Golden State Valkyries, Explorer Edition

If loving violet is wrong, we don't want to be right. We were absolutely delighted to see the Valkyries go all in on the violet colorway with their most recent Explorer Edition.

Violet—or any pastel for that matter—can go wrong if juxtaposed colors and patterns are either too harsh or too subtle. Golden State nailed the details, with tasteful gold accents throughout, and wings beneath the armholes to represent the flight of the Valkyries.

Wait, what did we say about the atrocity that is highlighter green? Forget that when it comes to Dallas-based teams—their city skyline is famously outlined by the color.

In a similar fashion, these Wings Rebel Editions are outlined by the green in all the right places, much like the literal usage of a highlighter pen. Turns out bright green is a whole lot more palpable with a purpose and correct usage.

We love a statement font as well, and this one screams "Texas." Yes, they look similar to the 2022-23 Mavericks City Connects, but they upgraded the concept and the font really seals the deal.

We're suckers for a pop of tasteful novelty, and the tiny basketball embedded in the latest Fever Rebel Editions takes them into the top three. Not only is the patch cute without being annoying, it's also a nod to the team's primary logo.

"Expect to win," the mantra of Fever legend Lin Dunn, is strewn across the shorts. It's a detail that showcases what the Fever do so well when it comes to uniforms: They blend the past, present and future together and mix in a ton of pride for the state of Indiana.

The Indy wordmark is a fun pop that accomplishes all of the above.

The Portland Fire went with an extremely bold homage to the City of Roses for their first-ever Rebel Editions, and boy, did they pull it off.

This isn't your typical rose-themed attire. Portland went with a more subtle pattern of gray roses that seamlessly blend in with the jersey's black background. They saved the red for the outlines and accents, and it all makes the color pop wonderfully. Even the green sponsor ad works to give the jersey a hint of vine to go with its roses.

The kicker is the font, completely leaning into a gothic vibe atypical for a basketball jersey in the best way. It's extra satisfying to see a new team take a risk and watch it pay off.

1. Los Angeles Sparks, Court Origins Edition

Did we mention that we're suckers for a pop of tasteful novelty?

No one has done this over the years better than the L.A. Sparks and their palm tree, and there was no better reminder that the Sparks have been the blueprint than this year's Court Origins Edition.

It's super fun and even a bit emotional to see the iconic teal palm tree worn by Lisa Leslie out there. It's also fun to see the retro design of the jersey itself—don't the length of it and the shoulders just take you right back to the '90s?

The Sparks are always at the top of jersey lists (or at least ours) for good reason: The purple-and-yellow color scheme is synonymous with the area, the palm tree is shameless and it's all somehow cool—just like L.A.

articles.title: La selección femenina sueña antes de poner rumbo al Mundial: "¿Por qué no el oro?"
articles.standfirst: España, ya con las 12 internacionales definitivas, se despide antes de viajar a Berlín
articles.summary: España, ya con las 12 internacionales definitivas, se despide antes de viajar a Berlín
articles.body: Antes de partir este martes hacia Berlín para la disputa del Mundial, la selección femenina se despidió en un acto en el que se alimentó la ilusión de tener un papel destacado en el torneo. "El oro, por qué no soñar, pero volveremos con un resultado del que nos sentiremos todos orgullosos", aseguró Elisa Aguilar, presidenta de la FEB. España no acude a la cita mundialista desde hace ocho años. La edición que arranca este viernes se presenta muy igualada y llena de incógnitas por la reciente incorporación de las jugadoras que militan en la WNBA, un hecho que afecta a muchos de los equipos participantes. Estados Unidos, Australia, Francia, Bélgica... Sobran aspirantes al podio. "Hay jugadoras y selecciones muy buenas, pero el problema que tienen es que no son nosotras. No hay ningún equipo mejor que vosotras juntas", dijo Aguilar. España se presentará en el campeonato con un currículum que dice que es la vigente subcampeona de Europa, casi oro tras perder una final ante Bélgica que estaba en la mano. También suma tres medallas en los últimos cuatro Mundiales (una plata en 2014 y dos bronces en 2010 y 2018), algo que en ese periodo de tiempo sólo han conseguido potencias planetarias como Estados Unidos y Australia. La selección, sin embargo, faltó a la última edición tras no lograr la clasificación en 2021. Horas antes se había hecho oficial la lista de las 12 internacionales que acudirán a la cita. Un equipo rebosante de talento, juventud y ambición con la destacada presencia de cinco jugadoras de la WNBA: Awa Fam, Raquel Carrera, María Conde, Alicia Flórez y Megan Gustafson, que será la última en incorporarse, ya en Berlín y sin apenas tiempo de entrenarse con el resto del grupo. "Habrá sólo tres entrenamientos antes del debut y hay que preparar la suma de las que ya estaban con las que han llegado", explicó el seleccionador Miguel Méndez, que va al equipo "preparado para disfrutar en cualquier escenario que haya durante los partidos". Alba Torrens, que este domingo cumplió 37 años y es la única que ha participado en un Mundial, ejercerá de capitana. "Es admirable su esfuerzo. Es la guardiana de lo que significa representar la camiseta de la selección", valoro la presidenta Aguilar. La alero ve un grupo que llega "con mucha ambición. Este equipo me ilusiona, me hace crecer y volver a soñar, aunque con humildad". España compartirá grupo con Alemania, Mali y Japón. Este viernes (17.45 horas) debutará ante la selección anfitriona en el encuentro más complicado de la primera fase. Durante la preparación ya le vencieron en un duelo a puerta cerrada. Este sábado, sin apenas descanso (11.30 horas) se medirá al combinado africano, al que recientemente barrió en otro de los amistosos. Para acabar, se las verá con Japón el lunes 7 (17.50 horas). Si la selección acaba primera y, como es previsible, Estados Unidos también, irían por el mismo lado del cuadro y podrían encontrarse en semifinales. El líder pasará directamente a cuartos de final evitando una peligrosa repesca de octavos en la que cada segundo de grupo se medirá a un tercero. En ese caso, España tendría que enfrentarse a Hungría, Corea del Sur, Nigeria o Francia, aunque las galas apuntan a ser primeras.

articles.title: A'ja Wilson, Kelsey Plum won't play for Team USA at 2026 FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup for health reasons
articles.summary: Team USA is looking for its fifth-straight win at the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup.
articles.body:
Two of the biggest WNBA stars won't take the court for Team USA in September. Las Vegas Aces star A'ja Wilson and Phoenix Mercury guard Kelsey Plum will not participate in the 2026 FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup due to injuries, USA Basketball announced Monday.

Plum and Wilson will be replaced by Sonia Citron and Kiki Iriafen of the Washington Mystics.

Wilson's absence comes as a bit of surprise, as the 30-year-old has played in all but three games for the Aces this season. The four-time MVP winner has once again put up MVP-caliber numbers, averaging 26 points, 9.4 rebounds and 3.2 assists.

While Wilson hasn't dealt with a significant injury this season, her decision to pass on the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup could be related to rest and workload.

In Plum's instance, a lower leg and calf injury has played a major role in her production this season. While the 32-year-old started off the season strong, the injury has limited both her availability and performance. Since joining the Mercury after a midseason trade, Plum has appeared in just five games with the team, and is averaging only 15.8 points, down from the 23.9 she averaged with the Los Angeles Sparks before the deal.

That injury won't just keep Plum out of the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup, it will also sideline her for the rest of the WNBA season, per ESPN.

While those losses will be felt, Team USA is still in good hands with the rest of its roster. After finishing second in the Rookie of the Year voting last season, Citron kept up that momentum in Year 2.

The 22-year-old is averaging 16.8 points and 4.3 assists. While her excellence from beyond the arc has taken a hit, she still managed to make the All-Star team for the second straight season.

Iriafen, 23, has shown growth in her second season in the league. She's averaging 15.3 points and 9.4 rebounds in 37 games.

That pair will join a star-studded Team USA roster that also features names like Caitlin Clark, Breanna Stewart, Napheesa Collier and Angel Reese, among other WNBA stars.

Team USA is looking to win its fifth straight FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup. Play begins Sept. 4 and runs through Sept. 13.

articles.title: A'ja Wilson, Kelsey Plum Out of FIBA World Cup for Health Reasons, USA's Updated Roster Revealed
articles.summary: USA Basketball announced Monday that Las Vegas Aces center A'ja Wilson and Phoenix Mercury guard Kelsey Plum won't compete in the 2026 FIBA Women's World Cup due to health reasons.
articles.body:
USA Basketball announced Monday that Las Vegas Aces center A'ja Wilson and Phoenix Mercury guard Kelsey Plum won't compete in the 2026 FIBA Women's World Cup due to health reasons.

The Washington Mystics' Sonia Citron and Kiki Iriafen will fill the two open spots in the 12-player squad.

Angel Reese breaks yet another WNBA record

Wilson is a significant loss. She's headed in all likelihood toward her fifth WNBA MVP, having averaged 26.0 points, 9.4 rebounds and 2.0 blocks through 37 games with Las Vegas.

The 30-year-old has been a standout performer for the national team as well. She was the MVP of the 2022 World Cup and 2024 Summer Olympics as the United States captured gold in both events.

Plum has battled injuries throughout the 2026 season and had to adjust to a new setting following her trade from the Los Angeles Sparks. She averaged 21.5 points and 5.4 assists in 17 appearances, with the Mercury confirming she's shut down for the remainder of the year.

Wilson and Plum's exits provide a silver lining as Citron and Iriafen are two young stars who could contribute to Team USA for many years ahead. They're both two-time All-Stars and have played critical roles in clinching Washington's first playoff berth since 2023.

It was only a matter of time before Citron and Iriafen represented the U.S. in a major tournament, so Monday's news hastened the inevitable.

Despite missing Wilson and Plum, the United States will still head into the World Cup as the favorite. It boasts more talent than any other country with a roster headlined by Paige Bueckers, Napheesa Collier and Caitlin Clark.

Team USA will tip off the tournament Friday against China.

articles.title: Wolves' Trey Kaufman-Renn fighting for NCAA return, emergency hearing Tuesday
articles.summary: Kaufman-Renn will appear before a judge in Clark County, Indiana, on Tuesday. He's attempting to play one more season of college basketball.
articles.body:
Trey Kaufman-Renn is seeking a sixth year of eligibility in the NCAA, meaning his short time with the Minnesota Timberwolves is over.

Minnesota selected the former Purdue star 59th overall in the 2026 NBA Draft. Kaufman-Renn has not signed a contract with the Timberwolves, but he participated in the NBA Summer League and joined the team for a bonding trip to France hosted by Rudy Gobert.

Court documents obtained by Bring Me The Sports show that Kaufman-Renn filed a motion for a preliminary injunction against the NCAA as he seeks a sixth year of eligibility.

Here's the specific wording in the motion:

Kaufman-Renn seeks a preliminary injunction requiring the NCAA, during the pendency of this action, to treat him as retaining one season of competition available for use during the 2026-2027 academic year, and restraining the NCAA during that period from applying or enforcing its eligibility rules and its transition classification to prevent him from enrolling at, transferring to, practicing with, or competing for a member institution during the 2026-2027 academic year, from invoking against him his entry into or selection in the 2026 NBA Draft, his professional representation, or his participation in the 2026 NBA Summer League, and from penalizing any member institution, conference, coach, or administrator for acting in accordance with the Court's order.

It might be a long shot for Kaufman-Renn, but his chances of earning a roster spot on a deep Timberwolves team were slim to none.

The NCAA's new age-based model disqualifies Kaufman-Renn from further college-level competition. It allows five years of eligibility beginning with their first academic year following their 19th birthday. Redshirt seasons and medical hardship waivers are no longer allowed.

Kaufman-Renn redshirted in 2021-22 at Purdue and then played the next four seasons. Under the new rules, he's exhausted his five years of eligibility.

The 2026-27 academic year is about to begin. The men's college basketball season begins in earnest in October, with games starting in November.

Kaufman-Renn's request for an emergency hearing was granted, and he will appear before a judge at 8:30 a.m. CT on Tuesday.
