articles.title: Jalen Brunson Reacts to Mitchell Robinson Signing Celtics Contract After Knicks' NBA Championship
articles.summary: The New York Knicks lost a key piece from their 2026 championship roster when veteran center Mitchell Robinson signed with the rival Boston Celtics in free agency.
articles.body:
The New York Knicks lost a key piece from their 2026 championship roster when veteran center Mitchell Robinson signed with the rival Boston Celtics in free agency.

While speaking to Stefan Bondy of the New York Post , Knicks star point guard Jalen Brunson addressed losing Robinson for the first time and admitted that it was "very tough" to see him walk this summer.

"Obviously playing for a rival and I know people want every team to hate each other. But there are some people you really care for and that's my guy," Brunson told Bondy. "I'm happy for him. And now, whenever we play him—four times a year—he's not my friend that day."

Robinson was the longest-tenured member of the Knicks roster last season, and his loyalty paid off as they won their first NBA championship since 1973. The big man's rebounding and interior defense helped New York dominate its opponents throughout the postseason.

The Knicks found a replacement for Robinson by signing veteran center Andre Drummond, so Brunson will have to get used to his new rim protector as the team tries to defend its title during the upcoming season.

articles.title: Estados Unidos se queda sin la jugadora más dominante del planeta a pocos días del Mundial
articles.standfirst: A'ja Wilson (tres títulos de la WNBA, cuatro MVP de la temporada regular, dos oros olímpicos y dos mundiales) y Kelsey Plum se pierden el torneo
articles.summary: A'ja Wilson (tres títulos de la WNBA, cuatro MVP de la temporada regular, dos oros olímpicos y dos mundiales) y Kelsey Plum se pierden el torneo
articles.body: Estados Unidos ha recibido dos varapalos en forma de ausencias a pocos días de que arranque el Mundial Femenino. La gran favorita al oro no podrá contar con la base Kelsey Plum ni con la pívot A'ja Wilson, dos grandes estrellas de la WNBA y piezas importantes en la selección. Sus lugares los ocuparán Kiki Iriafen y Sonia Citron. Sobre todo el hueco de Wilson es imposible de llenar. Desde su 1,93, se trata de la jugadora más dominante de los últimos años en el baloncesto mundial. Ahí están sus cuatro galardones de MVP de la WNBA (2020, 2022, 2024 y 2025), sus tres campeonatos con Las Vegas Aces, sus elecciones para el mejor quinteto de la competición, para el mejor quinteto defensivos, para el All Star... Con la selección estadounidense también se ha mostrado intratable. Acumula dos oros olímpicos, siendo elegida mejor jugadora en los Juegos de París, y otros dos oros mundialistas, consiguiendo también el MVP en la última edición celebrada hace cuatro años. La pívot ha sufrido leves lesiones de tobillo y espalda durante el curso en la WNBA y parece haber priorizado el descanso para llegar en plenitud a los playoffs de la Liga estadounidense. Con promedios de 26, puntos y 9,4 rebotes, también está inmersa en la carrera por conseguir un nuevo MVP de la temporada regular. Plum, mientras, ha estado lidiando con una lesión en la pantorrilla y, según ha informado su equipo, las Phoenix Mercury, ha sido descartada no sólo para el Mundial sino para lo que resta de campaña. Estaba promediando 21,5 puntos y 5,4 asistencias. Traspasada desde Los Angeles Sparks a primeros de agosto, la base sólo ha podido disputar cinco encuentros con su nuevo equipo. Dos bajas de peso para la selección estadounidense, que sigue siendo la gran favorita al oro en el Mundial, pero parece algo más asequible.

articles.title: Vidorreta le da a Perry los mandos del Unicaja
articles.standfirst: Primer amistoso del Unicaja con exhibición ofensiva: 67-105
articles.summary: Primer amistoso del Unicaja con exhibición ofensiva: 67-105
articles.body: El Unicaja estrenó la era Txus Vidorreta con una contundente victoria ante el Melilla Ciudad del Deporte (67-105) en el III Memorial Javier Imbroda. El conjunto malagueño dominó desde el inicio gracias a su velocidad ofensiva y a una intensa defensa que le permitió abrir rápidamente una amplia brecha en el marcador. Kendrick Perry fue el jugador más valorado del encuentro con 28 créditos, después de firmar 19 puntos y nueve asistencias. Entre los nuevos fichajes destacó especialmente Iggy Brazdeikis, autor de 20 puntos sin fallo, seis rebotes y tres asistencias. También dejaron buenas sensaciones Cameron Hunt y Simonas Lukošius, este último muy acertado desde el perímetro. El Unicaja no dio opción a la reacción melillense tras el descanso y llegó al último cuarto con una ventaja de 35 puntos (50-85). Los de Vidorreta mantuvieron el control hasta el final y superaron incluso la barrera de los 100 puntos para cerrar una primera prueba de pretemporada con una victoria clara y buenas sensaciones. El Unicaja dominó con claridad y Vidorreta terminó satisfecho con lo que vio. Especialmente con la predisposición de una plantilla que apenas lleva diez días de trabajo. "Fue un buen test. El equipo está atento a los conceptos que queremos utilizar y corriendo siempre que puede correr", explicó el entrenador, que valoró especialmente el ritmo mostrado por sus jugadores. "Hemos jugado con un ritmo alto. Hemos hecho muchos tiros, algunas veces con más acierto y otras veces con menos. Hemos sido capaces de mantener un equilibrio entre la defensa y el ataque, controlando las pérdidas", añadió. Una carta de presentación que encaja con el estilo que pretende implantar el nuevo técnico cajista.

articles.title: Latest Lakers Rumors Update Impact of $12.5B Sale on Rob Pelinka Hiring New Assistant GM
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Lakers' ongoing ownership saga might be hamstringing the front office, according to The Athletic's Dan Woike.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers' ongoing ownership saga might be hamstringing the front office, according to The Athletic's Dan Woike .

Woike reported Monday that some around the organization "have acknowledged that high-end positions, particularly in basketball operations, aren't actively being filled."

"That likely includes the assistant general manager position Rob Pelinka said the Lakers planned on hiring this offseason to handle personnel and scouting," per the report.

The Lakers hired Rohan Ramadas as their assistant general manager of strategy and data systems in May. That preceded their proposed $12.5 billion sale to a group led by Josh Kushner and Bob Iger.

Woike wrote that "it's not fully clear how or when the lead of much-needed pro scouting staff will be installed."

The sale to Kushner and Iger isn't official, so Mark Walter is still the majority stakeholder with Jeanie Buss recognized as the team governor for league business.

As a result, a lot of people behind the scenes are stuck in a holding pattern, and that includes Pelinka. Kusher and Iger may have their own ideas for the broad focus of the front office and how resources should be allocated once they come aboard.

While the situation isn't optimal for Pelinka, waiting a few more weeks or months to fill out his staff may not create a huge problem.

Los Angeles' roster is set heading into the 2026-27 season, and Pelinka took what are likely to be his biggest swings for the next few years. Re-signing Austin Reaves and acquiring Walker Kessler in a sign-and-trade ate up most of the Lakers' salary cap flexibility and trade assets.

Assuming they're in a contending position, the Lakers will presumably consider making some moves before the NBA trade deadline, though. Making the right upgrades around the margins can go a long way.

Pelinka will be at a disadvantage if the front office remains understaffed at a time when he needs to evaluate prospective targets.

articles.title: New Lakers Rumors Reveal Players, Staff Were 'Turned Off' by 'Arrogance' of Dodgers' Impact on Team
articles.summary: There are employees within the Los Angeles Lakers who reportedly aren't terribly upset by Los Angeles Dodgers' owner Mark Walter selling the team to Bob Iger and Josh Kushner for $12.5 billion.
articles.body:
There are employees within the Los Angeles Lakers who reportedly aren't terribly upset by Los Angeles Dodgers' owner Mark Walter selling the team to Bob Iger and Josh Kushner for $12.5 billion.

According to Dan Woike of The Athletic, "The pending changes—Iger and Kushner's groups are in their 'diligence' phase of the purchase—have certainly caused some anxiety for employees bracing for another ownership change. The last transition, from the longstanding familial touches of the Buss family to a more bottom-line-driven Walter regime, included multiple rounds of layoffs. Still, multiple sources in different departments expressed optimism about the direction of the franchise under Iger and Kushner. Some felt the Dodgers' impact on the Lakers was pushing too hard toward analytics and doing so with an arrogance that turned off some people in basketball operations and the locker room. Those people weren't upset to see a pathway for new management to come in, even if it's a bit of a mystery and doesn't have the track record of the Dodgers' success."

Walter officially purchased a majority stake in the Lakers in Oct. 2025, but his tenure lasted less than a year, and his sale to Iger and Kushner stunned the NBA world.

"People don't buy teams and turn around and sell them," an Eastern Conference executive told ESPN's Dave McMenamin earlier in August. " So there are obviously other factors driving this decision outside of just the mere fact that somebody showed up to pay $12.5 billion. Those factors have to be well outside of basketball."

Ultimately Walter turned a tidy $2.5 billion profit off his brief spell as the team's owner, though it sounds as if some folks within the basketball side of the organization won't be sad to see him go.

articles.title: Ridgefield woman who died on vacation to Wyoming ‘always found the good in everything," family says
articles.summary: "She wasn't known for changing the world except for loving her family... and I think she did that," Joe Griffin said of his wife Sandy.
articles.body:
RIDGEFIELD – Throughout more than two decades as a couple, Joe Griffin remembers his wife Sandra "Sandy" Griffin, who died Aug. 13 while on a family vacation in Wyoming , for her love of life and her family.

"She always found the good in everything," said Joe Griffin of Ridgefield. "She always found a reason to smile and always found something to celebrate, big or small. Sandy was a woman focused on her family and community, and the type of impact that she had has been noticed by the incredible outreach from not just locally but everyone that she touched."

Sandy Griffin died Aug. 13 at the age of 51 during a family vacation in Jackson Hole, Wyoming, according to her obituary. She is survived by her husband and their three children, among other family members, her obituary states.

Joe Griffin said their family was finishing a week-long dream vacation in Wyoming to celebrate his parents' 80th birthday at the time of his wife's death.

"We were on a 15-person family reunion, and she had a medical emergency on the last evening," he said.

Joe Griffin said he first met his wife through a "chance acquaintance" while they were out with a group of friends in Bryant Park in New York City. The park would later become the site where they got engaged, he said.

Recalling his first impression of his future wife, Joe Griffin said she was "a blonde knockout," adding, "I definitely wanted an opportunity to meet and speak with her, and it worked out that we were able to that night."

Joe Griffin said he was attracted to Sandy Griffin's love for life as well as her "infectious smile," her selflessness and her ability to give "the most out of every day." Out of their 20 years together, he said they were married for 18 years and raised three children together.

Prior to their marriage, Joe Griffin said his wife spent a decade in the fashion industry in New York City on the "business and operation side," where she worked with designers to bring their designs to life. He said she later gave up her career to focus on raising a family, and following the birth of their third child, they realized they "needed to find a community to make our own."

In the Ridgefield community, Sandy Griffin was involved in the PTA at both Veterans Park Elementary School and East Ridge Middle School and volunteered with a variety of local groups, including Soccer Club of Ridgefield, Ridgefield Basketball Association, Ridgefield Little League Baseball, the Ridgefield Baseball Booster Club and Kindness Over Muscular Dystrophy, her obituary said.

She also spent five years directing the annual Spring Variety Show at Veterans Park Elementary School, where she celebrated her final production this past May, according to her obituary. Joe Griffin said his wife's work with the Spring Variety Show was what she most known for, and the show became "a fixture for everyone in town."

Beyond her involvement in the Ridgefield community, Joe Griffin said his wife loved walking and being in the sunshine as well as spending time at the beach and ocean. He said many of their family vacations involved going to the beach, including trips to the Bahamas, Bermuda and Turks and Caicos and their honeymoon in South Africa.

Joe Griffin said the number of people who attended his wife's wake and funeral "speaks volumes to the person she was."

"She wasn't known for changing the world except for loving her family," he said. "That was her motto – 'If you want to change the world, go home and love your family' – and I think she did that."

Correction: This story has been updated to reflect Sandy Griffin died on Aug. 13.

articles.summary: El pívot estará tres meses alejado de las canchas por una fractura en su pie izquierdo
articles.body: Yannick Nzosa ha recibido este lunes la peor de las noticias en el inicio de la pretemporada del Unicaja. El pívot congoleño sufre una fractura del quinto metatarsiano del pie izquierdo, una lesión que le obligará a pasar por el quirófano esta misma semana y que podría mantenerle alejado de las pistas durante alrededor de tres meses. Nzosa se lesionó este domingo durante el encuentro amistoso disputado ante el Melilla Ciudad del Deporte, correspondiente al III Memorial Javier Imbroda. El interior cajista apenas pudo participar durante 3 minutos y 21 segundos, ya que sufrió un traumatismo en el pie izquierdo al comienzo del partido y tuvo que abandonar la pista sin posibilidad de regresar. A su llegada a Málaga este lunes, el jugador fue sometido a diferentes pruebas médicas en el Hospital Quirónsalud Málaga, que confirmaron los peores pronósticos: una rotura del quinto metatarsiano del pie izquierdo que requiere tratamiento quirúrgico. El jugador será intervenido a lo largo de esta semana. El periodo de recuperación dependerá de su evolución después de la operación, aunque la primera estimación apunta a unos tres meses de baja. Se trata de un importante contratiempo para Txus Vidorreta, que pierde durante buena parte del inicio de la temporada a uno de sus jugadores interiores justo cuando el equipo se encuentra en plena preparación para el nuevo curso.

articles.title: Angel Reese Turns Heads With Unapologetic Response to Viral Bikini Selfie
articles.summary: WNBA star Angel Reese addressed online critics head-on after facing backlash over swimsuit selfies posted to her social media. Refusing to apologize or chang...
articles.body:
WNBA star Angel Reese addressed online critics head-on after facing backlash over swimsuit selfies posted to her social media. Refusing to apologize or change her personal brand, Reese pushed back against public commentary about how female athletes choose to present themselves outside of basketball.

Reese defended her right to share lifestyle content without facing unwanted sexual attention. She also said fame can make people forget that she is still a young woman dealing with the pressure of public life.

Angel Reese responds to criticism over swimsuit photos

The comments came on "Unapologetically Angel," the podcast Reese hosts with co-host Maya Reese. The conversation started after co-host Maya Reese asked Angel for her take on people in the media and online who treat her confidence in her body as justification for sexualizing her.

Reese said she simply does not accept that logic. "I don't know what that means because I'm a beautiful woman, I've been posting pictures in my bikinis, I got a nice body, and I work hard for it," Reese said . "If I want to post a picture of my bikini, I should be able to without being sexualized where I'm saying I'm asking for it."

She made clear the criticism is not new, and she is tired of hearing the same argument recycled every time she posts. "It's been happening for a really, really long time, no, now, and now it's just like, okay, find something new," she said.

Reese also pointed to Skylar Diggins-Smith as an example of a player who built a massive following partly on the strength of her confidence and style. She wondered aloud whether Diggins would have faced the same scrutiny Reese does now, had social media been as powerful back then.

"I'm sure Skylar Diggins was posting pictures of her bikini. I'm running because she walked, she's the OG," Reese said. "Knowing that, I wonder if social media was at a high when she was popping, would she be going through the same thing when it comes to that? Being a beautiful woman who posts pictures and always looks good?"

She also brought up WNBA legends Lisa Leslie and Tina Thompson, both Hall of Famers who were known for their style throughout their careers. Reese noted that neither player became a national flashpoint for it, largely because the platform for that kind of pile-on did not exist at the time.

Angel Reese sees this as the WNBA's "Baddie Era"

Despite the toll the attention takes, Reese did not frame the entire conversation as negative. She sees the current moment in the WNBA as something genuinely worth celebrating, even if increased visibility comes with a darker side.

"It's popping right now. I'm happy to see all the girly girls being able to pop it and look cute on the runway and being able to continue that because we have a couple of models in this league, like we got some face cards," she said.

On the court, Reese is having the best season of her career. In her first year with the Atlanta Dream after two seasons with the Chicago Sky, she is averaging 16.1 points, 12.4 rebounds, 2.8 assists, and 1.8 steals across 40 games. She also set the WNBA single-season record with her 29th double-double of the year, breaking a record that had stood for years. The Dream sit first in the Eastern Conference at 26-14.

articles.title: Lexie Brown Sounds Off on ‘Disproportionate Respect’ From WNBA Owners in Pay Talks
articles.summary: Seattle Storm guard Lexie Brown spoke to Michael Porter Jr. about the low pay WNBA players faced early in their careers. Even as the No. 7 pick in the 2018 d...
articles.body:
Seattle Storm guard Lexie Brown spoke to Michael Porter Jr. about the low pay WNBA players faced early in their careers. Even as the No. 7 pick in the 2018 draft, Brown said she made about $40,000 in her rookie season, making it tough to live on basketball alone.

Like many other players, Brown played overseas during the offseason to earn more. As the WNBA grows, players continue to push for better pay and working conditions.

Lexie Brown speaks out about lack of respect in pay negotiation talks

For a long time, the money WNBA players made did not come close to matching what they were worth. Brown knows this better than most. She has been in the WNBA since 2018, when she came in as the seventh pick and still could not make ends meet on her salary.

"I made like 40k my rookie year. You can't live off 40k, so I took my a-s overseas immediately. I played for three straight years," Brown said on the Curious Mike podcast .

Brown also talked about the frustration players faced when negotiating with league owners. She described what that attitude felt like from where she was standing. "For them, we just felt like they just kept smacking us in the face. Like, 'Y'all are just asking for too much. Like we just need y'all to show up and play and just be happy with the little money that we're giving you,'" she said.

On top of that, players felt like they were being kept in the dark about what was actually happening in those meetings. Brown said the way information got passed down was part of the problem, and the lack of respect was obvious even in the small details: "It was crazy getting the information to us from their meetings with the ownership and then telling the player reps, and there was a very disproportionate level of respect."

Brown was not alone in seeking opportunities overseas during the offseason. Stars such as Diana Taurasi, Breanna Stewart and Brittney Griner also played abroad at different points in their careers. For many players, overseas basketball was an important way to make up for the limited income they received in the WNBA.

WNBA players were ready to walk away from games

Things started changing when the league began getting more attention. The rise of Caitlin Clark brought a whole new wave of fans, and the money coming into the WNBA started growing fast. Players figured that growth would show up in their paychecks. For a while, it did not. The league and commissioner Cathy Engelbert were slow to act, and that made players angry enough to organize.

When their demands were not met, they were prepared to take action together. Brown said they were ready to walk away from the game entirely if that was what it took.

"We stood on business. We didn't want to lock out, we didn't want to strike, but we were all completely prepared to. The league, they waited 'til the last possible moment, which was irritating, but they felt us. It's really an amazing, iconic, powerful thing that we were able to do as a league," she recalled.

The new CBA they won brought real changes, including better salaries, revenue sharing, and charter flights. Brown concluded by saying that the players never stopped loving the league, even when they were fighting it.

articles.title: Jonathan Kuminga's Agent Explains How Forward Was Hawks' 'Best Player' After Warriors Trade
articles.summary: Jonathan Kuminga's agent made a bold claim about his client's performance with the Atlanta Hawks.
articles.body:
Jonathan Kuminga's agent made a bold claim about his client's performance with the Atlanta Hawks.

Aaron Turner said on the Kevin O'Connor Show that Kuminga was the Hawks' best player in the second half of the season, citing the forward's net rating.

"He was their best player from the moment he showed up in terms of winning impact," Turner said (9:40 mark). "He had the best on/off net rating in the regular season and in the playoffs."

While a player's net rating is a good way to gauge how much of an impact he makes, to say that Kuminga was the Hawks' best player after being traded from the Golden State Warriors might be a bit of a stretch.

He certainly made an impact off the bench, putting up 12.3 points, 5.3 rebounds and 2.1 assists per game across 16 regular-season contests with the Hawks. He was even better in the postseason, averaging 13.7 points.

Still, most on the Hawks and those who went against them would likely point to a player like Jalen Johnson as the team's best player.

Turner's confidence in Kuminga is no surprise given that he's his agent, and it also explains his approach to the young player's free agency this offseason. Kuminga took longer than most to sign with a new team, and Turner was clearly eyeing a big contract.

Kuminga ultimately went with a two-year, $12.4 million contract with the Minnesota Timberwolves that includes a player option for 2027-28. That deal is actually significantly less than the one he received from the Los Angeles Lakers, who offered him $12 million-plus annually over three years, according to ESPN's Shams Charania .

Turner explained after the signing that Kuminga viewed Minnesota as a better fit.

Kuminga will look to break into a star role with the Timberwolves, but the team is likely just expecting solid production around Anthony Edwards. That might not stop Turner from calling Kuminga Minnesota's best player, though.

articles.title: 'Very Realistic' Karl-Anthony Towns, Josh Hart Take Discounts on Knicks Contracts, NBA Insider Says
articles.summary: Keeping a championship team together takes sacrifice from star players, and it appears the New York Knicks have two players willing to do so.
articles.body:
Keeping a championship team together takes sacrifice from star players, and it appears the New York Knicks have two players willing to do so.

Per The Athletic's James L. Edwards III , it is "very realistic" that Karl-Anthony Towns and Josh Hart take "discounts" this offseason, as neither will receive the max extensions they're eligible for.

Towns is eligible for a four-year extension worth $272 million, though it has been speculated for months that he won't end up signing for that much. Towns was a pivotal part of the Knicks' championship run, but it's fair to say that he isn't worth that kind of money at this point in his career.

Hart can sign a four-year, $132 million deal now, but Edwards reported earlier this month that those around the league see him signing a three-year deal with a range between $54 million and $62 million.

The Knicks lost one part of their championship core this summer when Mitchell Robinson signed with the Boston Celtics, but securing Towns and Hart for the next few years would help New York stay relevant in a competitive Eastern Conference.

articles.title: Stephen Curry Talks Warriors Future, Contract Talks amid Ahead of Final Year of Deal
articles.summary: Stephen Curry is entering the final season of his current contract, but he has no plans to leave the Golden State Warriors.
articles.body:
Stephen Curry is entering the final season of his current contract, but he has no plans to leave the Golden State Warriors.

"There's no question I want to be here the rest of my career, and I'm pretty sure that's going to happen," he said, per Dalton Johnson of NBC Sports Bay Area.

Johnson explained the future Hall of Famer is eligible to sign a maximum extension of two years and $136.7 million since he can no longer be under contract for more than three years due to the NBA's Over-38 Rule.

He is set to be the highest-paid player in the league on an annual basis at $62.6 million for the 2026-27 campaign.

"The deal and the contract stuff will happen at the right time, and we're not letting it be a distraction from our preparation for the season, and the fact that the team we're coming back with has a lot of familiarity," Curry said.

His long-term future figures to be a storyline since he is entering his age-38 season. What's more, injuries limited him to just 43 games during the 2025-26 campaign, which is a major reason the Warriors settled for the play-in tournament before their eventual elimination.

Golden State has players such as Jimmy Butler, Draymond Green and Kristaps Porziņģis on the roster heading into the 2026-27 season, but its overall ceiling will still depend on whether Curry can remain healthy and one of the best players in the league.

But even if he doesn't and the Warriors struggle to compete with the best teams in the Western Conference, it is difficult to imagine the all-time great suiting up for another team.

His resume includes four championships, two league MVPs, 11 All-NBA selections, 12 All-Star Game nods and a spot on the NBA's 75th Anniversary Team. He will forever be a Warriors legend and plans on remaining with the only NBA team he has ever known for the rest of his career.

articles.title: Mark Mitchell Will Stay at Missouri After Committing to Kentucky in CBB Transfer Portal
articles.summary: Forward Mark Mitchell will indeed be staying in college after a temporary injunction granted him a fifth season of college eligibility, though he won't be joining Kentucky as originally reported.
articles.body:
Forward Mark Mitchell will indeed be staying in college after a temporary injunction granted him a fifth season of college eligibility, though he won't be joining Kentucky as originally reported .

Instead, Mitchell will be re-enrolling at Missouri, per ESPN's Jeff Borzello:

Mitchell went through the NBA draft process and signed an Exhibit-10 contract with the Denver Nuggets, having exhausted his eligibility last season. But new NCAA rules this offseason allow players up to five years of eligibility within a five-year period, though Mitchell's class wasn't included in that ruling.

In response, Mitchell joined a lawsuit contesting his lack of eligibility. He and the other players in the case were granted a temporary injunction by Jefferson County Circuit Court Judge Brian Edwards.

Similar rulings elsewhere have cast a lot of uncertainty regarding eligibility and the transfer portal across the college football and basketball landscape:

Mitchell's return is a pretty huge one for the Tigers. The former Duke forward averaged 18.3 points, 5.3 rebounds and 3.6 assists for Missouri last season, shooting 54.7 percent from the field and 38.8 percent from three.

articles.title: Knicks projected to part ways with key 2026 NBA Championship piece
articles.summary: Due to James Dolan's decision to stay under the second apron, Jalen Brunson and the Knicks are set to lose a key piece of their 2026 NBA championship run - M...
articles.body:
A rare phenomenon in the NBA is when a team keeps its championship squad intact for a back-to-back run. The New York Knicks , led by Jalen Brunson, do not have that luxury heading into the 2026-27 season. They already lost Mitchell Robinson to the Boston Celtics ; the next domino is about to fall. That's because James Dolan has made it clear the franchise can compete, but only with certain salary cap stipulations. So, who's the person predicted to leave the Knicks? Miles McBride.

Knicks expected to part ways with McBride in 2026-27 NBA season

James Dolan has made things clear to Leon Rose: the Knicks can compete as long as their salaries do not hit the second apron. As a consequence, Jalen Brunson lost a screener and fair rebounder in Mitchell Robinson during the offseason. With this pattern looming, Miles McBride is the next candidate to leave.

The Knicks and McBride had an extension deadline in mid-August if they wanted him to settle for a cheaper deal. As expected, the young guard has not signed and will play out the last year of his deal with the Knicks. All signs point to the Knicks seeing McBride walk in NBA Free Agency and not getting any value in return, via James L. Edwards III of The Athletic.

"Unless the two sides reach an agreement before the start of the season, it feels like we're heading toward a departure just based on history... New York did great business in 2023 when it signed an unproven-but-talented McBride to a three-year, $13 million contract. The Knicks saw the development behind the scenes, and decision-makers figured they could get the second-round pick for a low price, while giving him some security. Since then, McBride has greatly outperformed this current contract," he declared.

Knicks fans now have to ask: how much was the disparity between McBride's performance and his contract?

His current deal with the Knicks is worth $13 million over three years, and he will earn $3,956,523 for the 2026-27 NBA season. This ranks him 300th among all players in the league by salary.

When looked at more deeply and compared to the players in the same salary range, McBride did way more and deserves a pay raise. In fact, he is slated to outperform his deal with the Knicks yet again if his Per 36 projections hold. (Numbers in bold indicate projected career-high averages)

Miles McBride 2026-27 Per 36 Minutes Projection

Rebuilding squads like the Brooklyn Nets , Sacramento Kings , and Memphis Grizzlies are all in the running to land McBride if he departs for a better deal before the next offseason. If the Knicks do want to give him a more competitive team to land on, they could also deal McBride to squads that are just a piece away from title contention like the Charlotte Hornets or Orlando Magic . Regardless, the Knicks, led by James Dolan and Jalen Brunson, will have to part ways with one of the most valuable bang-for-your-buck championship players in all of the league's history.

articles.title: Dwyane Wade celebrates major personal milestone with wife Gabrielle Union after 12 years of romance-filled bond: “I’m grateful for this view of her life”

articles.title: Contract Predictions for NBA's Best Extension-Eligible Players
articles.summary: With training camps opening in a month, the offseason is nearly over. Actual NBA basketball can't come soon enough, but teams still have business to attend to before opening night.
articles.body:
With training camps opening in a month, the offseason is nearly over. Actual NBA basketball can't come soon enough, but teams still have business to attend to before opening night.

Several top stars and prospects are eligible for contract extensions. Some will sign in the coming weeks; others will wait until the offseason. For the veterans heading into the final year on their contracts, the deadline isn't until the end of the year. First-round picks heading into their fourth season must sign before the regular season begins; otherwise, they'll face restricted free agency next July.

Let's break down the five most interesting candidates from each category!

After striking out on LeBron James, the Warriors face an awkward transition period with Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody recovering from serious injuries, an aging roster on short contracts, and a still-brilliant superstar in Steph Curry.

Curry is in the final year of his deal, earning the largest salary in the league at a staggering $62.6 million. The Warriors have the flexibility to pivot next season with massive cap space, but the franchise isn't likely to pivot away from Curry. The larger question would be finding the right salary to keep him happy, while giving the front office the means to retool around him.

Curry is already 38. The team can add two additional seasons to his deal for another $136.7 million, but will they offer that much, and does Curry want to explore a more ready-made contender for what may be his final years in the league?

Prediction: Pencil in Curry back with the Warriors, but at a discount closer to $100 million through 2028-29.

The long-running Giannis Antetokounmpo saga finally resolved with the Heat, landing the former NBA MVP in South Beach. Realistically, Miami wouldn't have pulled the trigger without assurances that Antetokounmpo would extend at the first, best opportunity.

The question isn't "will it happen?" but "When?" given Antetokounmpo is limited for six months from the July trade. As of October 1, Antetokounmpo can only add two additional seasons at about $135 million, which also assumes he opts into his $62.8 million for 2027-28, which is projected to be higher than his next-season maximum as a free agent.

Instead, expect a longer wait until January 8, when Antetokounmpo's extend-and-trade restriction lifts, allowing for a longer deal with higher raises.

Prediction: Antetokounmpo extends in early January, adding three years, $213.6 million.

The Denver Nuggets are in an odd spot as one of the top teams in the Western Conference each year, but not quite a contender since earning the title in 2022-23. From previously parting with veterans like Michael Porter Jr. and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope, to letting Peyton Watson go via sign-and-trade to the Cleveland Cavaliers this summer, the Nuggets seem to be squandering the best years of Nikola Jokić's career.

The three-time NBA MVP faces a situation similar to Giannis Antetokounmpo's, with a player option projected to exceed his max salary as a free agent next July. Jokić can opt in at $62.8 million and extend for almost $214 million for three additional seasons (through 2029-30).

Or, Jokić can wait until summer to opt out and re-sign for just under $360 million over five full seasons. The initial buzz has Jokić waiting, at least for now, to decide.

Prediction: Jokić doesn't extend, choosing to re-sign over the summer, with a non-zero chance he explores other opportunities, should the Nuggets continue to stagnate.

The Minnesota Timberwolves are another Western Conference contender, though unlike the Denver Nuggets, the franchise hasn't been able to break through to win a title. Instead, the team made a significant shift this offseason, sending big men Julius Randle and Naz Reid out, all while landing former All-Star point guard LaMelo Ball.

Whether it works or not is immaterial; the team's star remains Anthony Edwards, and Minnesota will pay whatever it takes to lock him into a new deal. Edwards can sign immediately, but he's limited to adding two years, $121 million. Despite his appeal, Edwards didn't reach the 65-game threshold to earn All-NBA honors, which would have opened the door to a much larger "supermax" extension.

Edwards waiting a year opens the door to a $300 million deal over four years, provided he stays healthy and continues to play at an elite level.

Prediction: No extension this offseason for Edwards, with an eye on the future windfall.

If the marriage between Karl-Anthony Towns and the New York Knicks was initially tenuous, the title run should cement the partnership for the long term. The larger question becomes budget, with team governor James Dolan likening the second apron to franchise suicide.

To win the title, the Knicks committed heavily to the core with Jalen Brunson, OG Anunoby, Mikal Bridges, Josh Hart, and Towns. Hart is also up for a new deal, with a team option for 2027-28 at $22.4 million. Instead, Towns owns a player option that is very close to next year's max salary at $61 million.

Will the Knicks commit to almost $273 million through the 2030-31 season, considering how many mouths the franchise needs to fill while avoiding the second apron?

Prediction: Towns extends with a lower starting number for 2027-28, in the $53.5 million range, paying up to $240 million over four seasons.

For the first rookie-scale entry on the list, representing the 2023 draft class, Keyonte George would have already signed a max deal were the Utah Jazz offering. Clearly, the team hasn't gone to that extreme to date.

George is eligible to add roughly $252 million over five additional seasons, or even $303 million should the team give him escalations for All-NBA, MVP, or Defensive Player of the Year. While Utah needs to be mindful of the $100 million it'll be paying Jaren Jackson Jr. and Lauri Markkanen together next season, the Jazz have yet to commit heavily anywhere else.

Last year, George put up tremendous numbers at 23.6 points and 6.1 assists a game, shooting 37.1 percent from three-point range on a solid 6.7 attempts per contest. Still, the team was relatively lousy, and he only made 54 appearances. Some of that had to do with the Jazz tanking for the draft lottery—recently addressed by NBA rule changes. Still, George is one of the league's more exciting young guards, and someone Utah should reinvest in.

Finding a viable number is the question, so he can avoid team-friendly restricted free agency.

Prediction: The Jazz and George compromise on a deal above $200 million over five years.

The Charlotte Hornets were one of the NBA's darling squads last season, coming on extremely strong in the second half of the season. The run ended with the play-in, but the Hornets had seemingly turned a corner, in part because of the play of Brandon Miller on the wing.

Then the franchise turned around two of its starting five in trades, sending LaMelo Ball to the Minnesota Timberwolves and Miles Bridges to the Phoenix Suns. Where does that leave Miller, who returned from injury that sidelined him for most of 2024-25 to play 65 games, averaging 20.2 points a night while shooting 38.3 percent from three on a heavy volume (8.2 attempts per game)?

The best case is a number both sides are comfortable with, but so far, no deal. The deadline for rookie-scale extensions is the day before the start of the regular season. Waiting for restricted free agency favors the team, but often sours the relationship and chemistry. Finding a compromise near the $200 million line over five years is the way to go.

Prediction: Miller and the Hornets reach an extension deal before the deadline, starting near $33 million for $191 million over five years.

On a team with Kevin Durant, Amen Thompson stood out last year as arguably the Houston Rockets' best player. For a non-shooter, Thompson is remarkably effective as a scorer, playmaker, and defender. The Rockets were just better when he was on the floor.

More importantly, Thompson represents Houston's future, whereas Durant, who will quickly join the Hall of Fame after he retires, will be 38 before the start of the season. How does all that translate into a starting salary in an extension? So far, it hasn't, but many rookie-scale deals don't get done until the October deadline.

Houston may be stubborn enough to take Thompson to restricted free agency, but hopefully both sides will find a deal.

Prediction: A five-year agreement for Thompson, with broad potential, but difficult to call, somewhere between $165 million and $200 million.

Twin brother of Amen Thompson, Ausar has become an integral part of the Detroit Pistons' resurgence. While he's not nearly as effective a scorer as his brother—neither shoots the three-ball well—Ausar is the better defender, elite enough to earn All-NBA All-Defensive First Team honors.

Elite offensive players tend to earn more than those who thrive on defense. The Pistons have also shown a willingness to wait on key players like Jalen Duren, who didn't extend last year and, as an All-Star through 2025-26, remains a restricted free agent.

That doesn't bode well for Thompson, who may have to wait if he's seeking too rich an extension. A compromise should start somewhere in the $20-$27 million range.

Prediction: The Pistons make Thompson wait until next summer.

The Orlando Magic have invested heavily in a roster designed to win now, yet the team has struggled to stay healthy enough to go deep into the playoffs. With investments in Paolo Banchero, Franz Wagner, Desmond Bane, Jalen Suggs and Wendell Carter Jr., this tax-adverse franchise may not have the flexibility to compensate Anthony Black before the October deadline adequately.

Black has great size for a guard, defends, and has grown significantly as a scorer. Still, with Bane and Suggs earning over $71 million for 2027-28, can Black displace either in the starting lineup? The Magic may not be able to afford him as a reserve at the price Black would seek, likely over a $20 million starting salary. Equally, the team should be hesitant to trade an important piece of their contending squad when waiting until restricted free agency is a viable option.

Prediction: No extension for Black, as the Magic wait until July of 2027 to decide his fate.

The list of players who will negotiate throughout the rest of the summer—some all the way through the June deadline—is long.

A few top names include Kawhi Leonard, assuming the LA Clippers clear the NBA Aspiration investigation and the trade to the Toronto Raptors is finally executed. The Milwaukee Bucks can extend recently acquired Tyler Herro; the rebuilding Brooklyn Nets have the option to extend Michael Porter Jr. Others include Jaylen Brown (Philadelphia 76ers), Tyrese Haliburton (Indiana Pacers), Anthony Davis (Washington Wizards), LaMelo Ball (Minnesota Timberwolves), and Zion Williamson (New Orleans Pelicans).

Additional rookie-scale-extension candidates are Scoot Henderson (Portland Trail Blazers), Cason Wallace (Oklahoma City Thunder), Jaime Jaquez Jr. (Bucks), Brandin Podziemski (Golden State Warriors), and Dereck Lively II (Dallas Mavericks), among others.

Email Eric Pincus at eric.pincus@gmail.com and follow him on X @EricPincus and Bluesky .

articles.title: Caitlin Clark Leaves WNBA Out of Top Spot as She Ranks Her Top 6 Career Moments
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark’s short career has already amassed enough historic milestones to make ranking her accomplishments difficult. However, when Clark was asked to r...
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark's short career has already amassed enough historic milestones to make ranking her accomplishments difficult. However, when Clark was asked to rank her most iconic moments, she answered without hesitation, placing the top spot.

During a recent promotional video with State Farm, Clark was asked to blindly rank six moments from her career as the interviewer listed them off. The first moment she was asked about was her breaking the NCAA scoring record, and she was clear about where it landed.

"I can't start with number one, can I?" she joked in the clip, which was posted to X . "I think I'm gonna put it at number one."

The moment came on February 15, 2024, when Clark surpassed Kelsey Plum's NCAA record for most career points in women's basketball against Michigan. The game itself was outstanding, with Clark scoring 49 points, including a signature deep three-pointer to break the record, something which became one of the defining images of her career with the Iowa Hawkeyes.

For Clark, that achievement ranked above any of the other moments she was asked about, all of which were after she entered the WNBA.

Her second choice was winning the Rookie of the Year award back in 2024. After being selected #1 overall by the Indiana Fever, she started an amazing rookie year, finishing with averages of 19.2 points and a league-leading 8.4 assists, setting the rookie single-season record for both categories: 769 points and 337 assists.

The third moment was Clark's first WNBA triple-double, which came on July 6, 2024. Against the New York Liberty, she finished the game with 19 points, 12 boards, and 13 dimes, becoming the first rookie and the youngest player ever to record a triple-double, doing so at the age of 22.

The previous youngest player to do so was Sabrina Ionescu, who recorded hers at age 23. The two played against each other during the game, matching up directly, but Ionescu outscored her, logging 22 points on 9-23 shooting, but it wasn't enough, as the Fever took the 83-78 win.

"This was a fun game," Clark said during the video as she reminisced.

Her fourth choice was her first All-Star appearance. As a refresher, the 2024 All-Star Game featured a group of All-Stars facing Team USA ahead of the Paris Olympics. It was praised for being one of the most competitive games in recent memory, with Team WNBA eventually taking a 117-109 win. Clark finished that game with four points and 10 assists.

At fifth place, Clark dropped the time she reached 1,000 points in her WNBA career. This time, she had an explanation behind her thought process.

"I didn't even know that when it happened," she claimed.

Clark reached that milestone in her third season, during the season opener against the Dallas Wings on May 9. She became the sixth-fastest player to reach the milestone, doing so in 54 games. She was also the fastest player to record 1,000 points and 500 assists, which she accomplished later that season.

In last place, Clark put her WNBA debut, which she thought "didn't go too hot."

She's not wrong. Clark started her career with a loss to the Connecticut Sun on May 14, 2024, and despite scoring 20 points, it was not a pretty sight. Clark shot 5-15 from the field and 4-11 from three, and finished with 10 turnovers, the most in a debut in league history.

"Honestly, that ended up in a good spot, so I'm not mad at it," she said after the list concluded. "That's a really good list. Honestly, probably where I would have put all of them."

Though her professional career is already filled with highlights, Clark is only getting started, and with many years ahead of her, the list could look very different by the time her career ends.

articles.body:
Having already three former NBA players this summer, Spanish giants Barcelona are reportedly about to add a fourth. Former Portland Trail Blazers wing Justin Minaya is set to continue his career in Europe, with Barcelona said to be closing in on a deal to add the 27-year-old to its extensively rebuilt roster.

According to multiple reports out of Spain and Europe, Barcelona is finalising an agreement with Minaya, with all indications being that the move is at an advanced stage. The signing is expected to be formally announced in the coming days and would give Minaya his first experience playing professionally in Europe, after three seasons in Portland, and four as a pro.

Minaya spent parts of three NBA seasons with Portland between 2022 and 2025, appearing in 57 games, and averaging ten minutes per contest. Although he never became a regular part of the rotation, his defensive ability helped him repeatedly earn opportunities with the franchise while spending much of his time on two-way contracts.

Across those 57 NBA appearances, Minaya averaged 1.7 points and 1.4 rebounds per game, shooting 31.4% from the field and 23.9% from three-point range. His most substantial NBA role came during the 2023-24 season, when he appeared 34 times and averaged 11.2 minutes per game, earning time for his defensive impact. Offensive limitations prevented him from earning a permanent rotation role, but Minaya established considerably more value through his work on the unglamorous end.

At 6'5 with a decent wingspan, Minaya has the size and physicality to defend multiple perimeter positions, thriving in the passing lanes while also able to step up to play impactful point-of-attack defense against opposing ball-handlers of all types and sizes. His rebounding, activity and ability to generate steals have been consistent features of his game, and that reputation was established before he reached Portland .

Minaya played four college seasons at South Carolina before using his additional year of eligibility at Providence in 2021-22. He averaged 6.5 points and 5.5 rebounds for a Friars team that went 27-6, won the Big East regular-season title and reached the Sweet 16 of the NCAA Tournament. Minaya went undrafted in the 2022 NBA Draft anyway, as befits a fifth-year senior with no obvious shot profile at the next level, but he played his way in anyway. Coaches, as always, love willing defenders.

Minaya initially played Summer League basketball with the Charlotte Hornets before joining the Mexico City Capitanes of the G League. During his first professional season, he averaged 8.2 points , 3.9 rebounds, 1.9 assists and 1.9 steals in 32.4 minutes per game, finishing tied for third in the G League with 57 steals and tied for 11th with 37 blocked shots. Portland signed him to a 10-day contract in April 2023, and that brief audition was enough to keep him within the organisation.

After Portland established the Rip City Remix as its own G League affiliate the following season, the Remix acquired Minaya's returning-player rights from Mexico City in October 2023. The Blazers subsequently signed him to a two-way contract, beginning a two-season spell in which he moved regularly between Portland and the G League, and re-signed him to another for the 2024-25 season.

Minaya's NBA opportunities, however, diminished during his final season with the Blazers. He appeared 19 more times in 2024-25 but averaged only 5.3 minutes, scoring 0.9 points per game. He shot 38.1% from the field but only 20.0% from three, and Portland did not retain him. Back to the G League for a fourth season in 2025-26 – but this time, without a two-way deal – Minaya spent time with the Orlando Magic before playing for their affiliate, the Osceola Magic, but posted career-low numbers across the board. As impressive as the defense could be, the offensive improvements never came.

If completed, Minaya will become the club's 11th addition of the summer. Barcelona has already added Justin Robinson, Umoja Gibson, Agustín Ubal, Stanley Umude , Tyrese Martin , Tosan Evbuomwan , Yoan Makoundou, Olivier Nkamhoua, Olek Balcerowski and Josh Nebo as part of a near-total reconstruction under head coach Aleksander Sekulic.

The club had previously been expected to use its final addition on another interior player, but the arrival of Makoundou changed that plan. Minaya instead gives Barcelona another athletic wing for a roster being constructed around greater pace, physicality and defensive versatility. Minaya also has an important administrative advantage; born in New Jersey, he is the son of former New York Mets general manager Omar Minaya and holds a Dominican passport, allowing him to qualify under the Cotonou agreement and therefore not occupy one of Barcelona's limited non-EU roster places in Spain's Liga Endesa. The move could be the start of a decade-long high-level European and/or Spanish career as a result.

Minaya was good enough defensively to remain on the Blazers' radar for three seasons, but his shooting – particularly his career 23.9% mark from three in the NBA from a primary shooting position – made it difficult to establish a larger role. At Barcelona, though, there should be less pressure on Minaya to supply offence and greater scope to use the defensive attributes that have sustained his professional career. After four seasons moving between the Trail Blazers and the G League, Minaya now appears ready to exchange that uncertainty for a significant role with one of Europe's biggest clubs. As well he should.

articles.title: Osaka channels NBA icon Iverson to reach US Open second round
articles.summary: Naomi Osaka channelled NBA fashion trailblazer Allen Iverson on Monday as she battled into the second round of the US Open."For me he's a trailblazer," Osaka...
articles.body:
Naomi Osaka channelled NBA fashion trailblazer Allen Iverson on Monday as she battled into the second round of the US Open.

The Japanese 13th seed, US Open champion in 2018 and 2020, was made to work hard by Russia's Anastasia Zakharova before winning 7-6 (8/6), 7-6 (7/3) in just over two hours on the Arthur Ashe Stadium show court.

As ever, Osaka's entrance on court grabbed the headlines, with the 28-year-old walking out in a billowy custom-made gown which contained sewn-in news clippings detailing her career.

The four-time Grand Slam champion also had her hair braided in the style of former Philadelphia 76ers star Iverson, the NBA icon who is often credited with helping bring street culture and style to basketball.

Osaka had paid tribute to Iverson in her pre-tournament press conference last week, wearing a t-shirt depicting the NBA star as she spoke to reporters.

"For me he's a trailblazer," Osaka said. "He's kind of like done a lot in fashion, whether it's on purpose or not, but he's shifted the way that NBA players dress.

"I also think the whole conversation around clothes in sports and also just expressing yourself through style, I feel like he's someone that I look up to in that regard."

Osaka needed to emulate Iverson's famously fierce competitiveness to finally subdue Zakharova.

She looked to be cruising to a routine first-round win after going 5-2 up in the opening set before Zakharova hit back to force a tiebreak.

Osaka recovered though to close out the set.

Another erratic second set from Osaka saw Zakharova recover from 5-3 down to level at 5-5, before holding for a 6-5 lead.

Osaka's powerful service game proved the difference though and she held to love before overwhelming Zakharova in the tiebreak.

articles.title: El pacto de vida de Stephen Curry: el plan del Rey Midas de la NBA para seguir cubierto de oro
articles.standfirst: Stephen Curry, que ha ganado 473 millones de dólares en su carrera en la NBA, quiere seguir en los Warriors y opta a un contrato de dos años más y 136,7 millones
articles.summary: Stephen Curry, que ha ganado 473 millones de dólares en su carrera en la NBA, quiere seguir en los Warriors y opta a un contrato de dos años más y 136,7 millones
articles.body: El Stephen Curry (38 años), que juega en los Golden State Warriors desde que fue drafteado con el número 7 en 2009, ha compartido su deseo de renovar con el equipo californiano. "No cabe duda de que quiero estar aquí el resto de mi carrera, y estoy bastante seguro de que así será", declaró a 'NBC Sports Bay Area' el cuatro veces campeón de la NBA y dos veces MVP. Stephen Curry, que se prepara para disputar su decimoctava temporada en la NBA, tiene contrato vigente hasta la temporada 2026-27 de la NBA por un valor de 62,6 millones de dólares, lo que lo convierte en el jugador mejor pagado de la NBA en términos de salario anual. Debido a la norma de la NBA para mayores de 38 años, Curry sólo puede firmar contratos con una duración máxima de tres años. El acuerdo máximo que puede suscribir ahora es por dos años y 136,7 millones de dólares. Respecto a su renovación apuntó en el Palo Alto Hills Golf & Country Club que "lo relacionado con el acuerdo y el contrato llegará en el momento oportuno; no permitiremos que eso distraiga nuestra preparación para la temporada". La temporada pasada resultó muy decepcionante para Stephen Curry y los Warriors, que terminaron el curso con 37 victorias y 45 derrotas. "Ojalá podamos mantenernos sanos y tener la oportunidad de demostrar de qué somos capaces; yo incluido, tras haberme perdido tantos partidos el año pasado", reconoció Curry, que el pasado curso promedió 26,6 puntos en los 43 partidos que pudo disputar. "El objetivo sigue siendo el mismo... Ya veremos lo de la extensión de contrato en el momento oportuno. Pero estoy listo para mi decimoctava temporada. Es increíble que haya pasado tanto tiempo y que siga intentando jugar a un nivel muy alto para ayudar al equipo a ganar; estoy preparado para cumplir con mi trabajo", compartió.

articles.title: El histórico Bosna Sarajevo vuelve a Europa por la puerta grande
articles.standfirst: El legendario equipo bosnio, campeón continental en 1979, sustituto del AS Monaco en la Eurocup
articles.summary: El legendario equipo bosnio, campeón continental en 1979, sustituto del AS Monaco en la Eurocup
articles.body: La EuroCup rescata a un gigante del baloncesto europeo. El Bosna BH Telecom Sarajevo ocupará la plaza del AS Mónaco en la Eurocup 2026-27 después de que el conjunto monegasco haya sido declarado no elegible por incumplir los requisitos establecidos en la normativa de la competición. El relevo devuelve al escenario continental a uno de los nombres míticos de la historia del baloncesto europeo. El Bosna regresa a la EuroCup 19 años después de su última aparición, dispuesto a recuperar el protagonismo que un día le convirtió en campeón de Europa. El equipo de Sarajevo, vigente campeón de Bosnia y Herzegovina, compartirá el Grupo D con Bahcesehir College Istanbul, Balkan Botevgrad, Manresa, Lietkabelis, PAOK, ratiopharm ulm y Roma Basketball. Su regreso será inmediato: el 30 de septiembre, en la pista del Lietkabelis. Han pasado exactamente 6.791 días desde su última presencia en la competición. Una espera interminable para un club que conoce de sobra lo que significa tocar la gloria europea. Porque el Bosna no es un recién llegado. Es historia pura del baloncesto continental. El 5 de abril de 1979 protagonizó una de las mayores gestas que se recuerdan al derrotar al Varese (96-93) en la final de la Copa de Europa disputada en Grenoble. Con una leyenda como el exmadridista Mirza Delibasic como gran referente y Zarko Varajic desatado —45 puntos en la final, récord histórico en un partido por el título de la máxima competición europea—, el conjunto yugoslavo se convirtió en el primer club de la antigua Yugoslavia en levantar la Copa de Europa. Y su última aventura en la EuroCup tampoco pasó precisamente desapercibida. En diciembre de 2007, el Bosna y el ALBA Berlín protagonizaron el partido más largo de la historia del torneo: 141-127 después de cinco prórrogas. Kyle Hill disputó 53 minutos y 18 segundos y cinco jugadores bosnios superaron los 40 minutos. El equipo incluso avanzó a las eliminatorias antes de caer ante el Gran Canaria. Ahora, casi dos décadas después, el Bosna vuelve a Europa. Un gigante dormido que vuelve a escena.

articles.title: Jilson Bango regresa al Casademont Zaragoza para reforzar su juego interior
articles.standfirst: El pívot de 2,08 m y 27 años firma contrato hasta el final de la temporada
articles.summary: El pívot de 2,08 m y 27 años firma contrato hasta el final de la temporada
articles.body: El Casademont Zaragoza ha alcanzado un acuerdo con Jilson Bango (2,08 metros, 1999) para que el jugador angoleño regrese a la disciplina rojilla hasta el final de la temporada 2026-2027, informó este martes el club aragonés. El pívot se encuentra en la fase final de su lesión en la rodilla izquierda, para la que necesita una última operación que será practicada en Zaragoza y cuya recuperación supervisarán los servicios médicos del Casademont Zaragoza. Cuando reciba el alta, el jugador se incorporará a la dinámica del equipo. Con este regreso vuelve a la capital aragonesa un jugador que, como destacó el comunicado de la entidad rojilla, maravilló a la afición y se convirtió en una de las grandes sensaciones de la Liga Endesa. Antes de recalar en el Fenerbahce turco, Jilson Bango registró con el Casademont Zaragoza unas medias de 13,4 puntos, 5,5 rebotes y 16,1 de valoración por encuentro en la ACB.

articles.title: Damian Lillard Shares Photo After Achieving Goal of 100K Shots Made in 1 Year Amid Injury Rehab
articles.summary: It turns out Damian Lillard's shooting clinic that the Portland Trail Blazers posted about last week represents only a small fraction of what he has been doing as he looks to return to the court in peak form after missing the entire 2025-26 season.
articles.body:
It turns out Damian Lillard's shooting clinic that the Portland Trail Blazers posted about last week represents only a small fraction of what he has been doing as he looks to return to the court in peak form after missing the entire 2025-26 season.

Lillard revealed on his Instagram Story that he set a goal of making 100,000 shots in one year as part of his rehab process, starting on Sept. 1, 2025, and he surpassed it over the weekend.

The start date was just over four months after Lillard tore his Achilles in a playoff game for the Milwaukee Bucks. He had surgery to repair the injury on May 2, so he was already back in the gym getting up shots within four months.

Lillard, who returned to the Portland Trail Blazers as a free agent last summer, sat out all of last season. There has been no official word from the team about his availability when training camp opens on Sept. 29, but his recent social-media posting suggests he's ready to get back at it.

articles.title: Former Dallas Mavericks Coach Compares Cooper Flagg’s Career Trajectory to LeBron James, But There’s a Caveat
articles.summary: Former Dallas Mavericks head coach Jason Kidd strongly believes Cooper Flagg is on his way to greatness after having coached him last season. After winning t...
articles.body:
Former Dallas Mavericks head coach Jason Kidd strongly believes Cooper Flagg is on his way to greatness after having coached him last season. After winning the NBA's Rookie of the Year award in April, Flagg enters the 2026-27 campaign with high expectations.

The 19-year-old swingman averaged 21.0 points, 6.7 rebounds, 4.5 assists, and 1.2 steals on 46.8 percent shooting from the field across 70 regular-season appearances for the Dallas Mavericks. During a recent interview with ALL-STAR Magazine, Kidd used LeBron James as Flagg's reference point.

"I think he's on pace when you talk about LeBron and what he did as a young player, and then also Cooper's ability," Kidd said of Flagg. "He's one that loves to win, wants to win, likes to work, is not afraid of the moment. We saw at Duke taking a game-winning shot and missing. He's not afraid of the moment. So I would say he is on pace. I think that's his comp."

"Now, can he stay healthy like LeBron? And then I think all greats are judged with championships. Not so much stats, but that's the one stat that will stand out, and hopefully Cooper can achieve that," he continued.

Dallas Mavericks News: Cooper Flagg named NBA's best 19-year-old

The Dallas Mavericks may have won only 26 regular-season games last season, but Cooper Flagg was a bright spot for the team. As his former coach Jason Kidd mentioned, the sky is the limit for Flagg.

In a recent Bleacher Report article by Andy Bailey, Flagg was named the NBA's best 19-year-old, as the Dallas Mavericks swingman beat out the likes of incoming rookies AJ Dybantsa, Darryn Peterson, and Cameron Boozer.

"His developmental arrow is already darn-near vertical. As a rookie, he averaged 18.8 points and 4.1 assists in his first 43 games. And from that point to the end of the campaign, he was at 24.7 points and 5.1 assists." Bailey said of Flagg.

"Flagg may have to cede some touches to Kyrie Irving this season, but his return will also divert some defensive attention away from him too. And that could help Flagg maintain the kind of production he had at the end of 2025-26," he continued. "As promising as the trio below is, they won't consistently reach those heights as rookies.
